Question: Can Skirmishers add stuff change their facing during a move? Can they change direction? How do they charge? And how does forming up work with Skirmishers?
Ruling:
Normal Movement and Marching
Skirmishers may remove stuff after this freely direction and pivot during normal movement and marching.

Charging with Skirmishers
During a Charge, they follow the charge criteria, therefore may change direction only once and must follow the shortest path to the closest visible model in the target unit.

The closest model in the charging unit moves first:
•    A single pivot must be made as early as possible in order to contact the nearest model in the charged unit via the shortest route.
•    Move straight, with your front facing directly forward, into base contact.

Charging Skirmishers with Skirmishers
The first moving model forms the center of the fighting rank upon contact. Other charging models have to form up (see below) in even numbers to the left and the right of that model. Maximum one model may be added in excess to that unevenly to one side. Against skirmishers you maximize only against the first contacted model of the enemy unit; adjust the path of the first charging model if it brings more of your models into base contact with the first contacted model. You do not have to alter your charge path in order to maximize the number of models in the enemy unit's fighting rank.
Skirmishers Charging formed units
When charging formed units, each model charges individually to form up (see below) to the charge target and form the fighting rank, so they can actively maximize base contact. Therefore, you have to prioritize base contact over the shortest route.

Units in Formed Formations (Open Order, Close Order etc.) charging Skirmishers
Any unit charging a unit of Skirmishers must take the shortest route to contact the closest visible model. The Skirmishers then form up (see below).

Forming Up (as charger against the enemy unit, building the fighting rank or if charged)
During Forming up, Skirmish models move in an order of their controlling player's choosing. They may move through friendly models and may pivot (once if charging). They form up edge to edge, front corner to front corner against the enemy fighting rank or behind if they have not sufficient movement. No model may move further than their M value, or their M value + the charge roll when charging. All Models unable to fully reach their required position in the ranks are removed as casualties (if the first model contacted is removed, others can still try to form up).

Question: The Fighting Rank. How do you determine the number of attacks of a model with closing in and stepping forward? How does the new FAQ, affect this? How are casualties removed in combat? How does this affect the number of attacks a unit can make?
Ruling:
Which models can attack and the number of attacks those models can make is determined in step 1.1. Per the combat phase sequence (as this step is not repeated) this is not revisited and largely does not change during a fight (this is also known as the "Combat Lock" or "Combat Freeze"). The FAQ about Press of Battle and Stepping forward from a fighting rank into another creates a clear exception to this norm: Models that were already in a fighting rank and determined to have been able to fight in step 1.1., can still make any remaining attacks they have after stepping up as they are closing in. In addition, if stepping up and closing in brought them into base to base contact with the enemy they may make their full number of attacks rather than just a singular attack  in order to  "maximizing their number of attacks".

For all other cases, the number of attacks is not changed when models Step Forward, move to replace characters that retire from the Fighting Rank, or change position in the unit due to shrinking units or other reasons.

Casualties are removed among models that can fight (within M") and from the ends of each rank (owner chooses from which end for every casualty):
- Firstly, from the first fighting rank,
- secondly, from the second fighting rank (if applicable),
- thirdly, from models making supporting attacks (if applicable),
- finally from models of the unit that cannot fight.
Remove actual models from the rear (mark the models counting as casualties). Once you removed your first casualty and if the back rank is incomplete, you must continue to remove models from the same direction in the rear rank.

Remember that a model that steps up into a different fighting rank due to casualty removal must allocate its attacks only against an enemy unit that it could have attacked prior to stepping up and models that step up into fighting ranks from outside cannot attack t all (as determined in 1.1)

Question: When using Evasive, how does it interact with Targeting, Magic Missiles, Bombardment, Cannon Fire and Line of Sight?

Evasive can be used after a  unit has been targeted by shooting. If the unit evades out of LOS or out of range, the attacks are lost. The following exceptions and special cases apply:
- Bombardment: You Target the unit by placing the template over it. If the unit uses Evasive, the template will not move with the unit, but will be resolved at the initial positon.
- Cannon Fire: If you target the enemy model, and the model moves by using evasive, the model and the target point are still separate entities. The shot will always be conducted from the target point.
- Magic Missiles: Use evasive before the casting roll is even made, after the target is announced. The wizard then may chose to not make the casting roll. ("unit may continue with its shooting as declared")

Question:
Can the rules Shield of the Lady and Verminous Valour, which both allow a character to ‘retire’ by ‘moving through the ranks’, be used outside of combat? These rules specify they can be used 'at any time', but also directly refer to 'the fighting rank' and 'the combat', and the rule for 'moving through the ranks’.

When must retired characters (from Refusing a Challenge, Too Many Characters, Shield of the Lady or Verminous Valour) "un-retire", a.k.a. return to their original (front rank) position?

What happens when a unit falls below Unit Strength 10 after a Handmaiden retires to the rear rank of that unit?
Ruling:
These rules directly refer to 'the fighting rank' and 'the combat' which only apply in combat, and involve 'moving through the ranks' which requires the unit to be engaged and the character to return to its original position as soon as it disengages: Unretire when the unit is not engaged in the current combat anymore, provided that that combat does not continue due to a Follow Up or Pursuit move (GW FAQ confirmed that an ongoing challenge continues in that case).

Note that you cannot use it as a reaction on already stated or announced actions. This means while resolving a combat you have to use it at the end of an initiative step, before targets of models' attacks are announced. You can use it outside of resolving the combat at any time, given the unit is engaged in combat.

Note that the Unit Strength 10 condition for shield of the Lady is checked at the moment the Handmaiden retires to the rear rank. If the condition is met at that time, the Lady’s effects remain active until the combat ends, even if the unit later falls below Unit Strength 10.

Question: Against which models do the various instances of Hatred (X) apply?
Ruling:
Some instances of Hatred are keyword-based, applying against models identified by a given keyword appearing on their Unit Card or in one of their Special Rules. These are: enemy Characters (Troop Type), enemy Wizards (typically identified in the Magic section of the Unit Card), Undead models (models with either the Nehekharan Undead or Necromantic Undead special rule), Daemonic models (models with the Daemonic special rule), and Daemons of Slaanesh/Tzeentch/Nurgle/Khorne (models with the corresponding Daemon of... special rule).

Other instances are faction-based, applying against all models belonging to a given faction. In several cases, the rules use legacy Warhammer Fantasy Battles faction names as shorthand (or as an unchecked carryover): Orcs & Goblins (Orc & Goblin Tribes), Dwarfs (Dwarfen Mountain Holds), High Elves (High Elf Realms), Empire (Empire of Man), Beasts of Chaos (Beastmen Brayherds).

Units taken as Mercenaries or Allies belong only to their own faction (if any) for the purposes of Hatred. By contrast, if a unit is fielded as part of another faction's Army Composition List (excluding Mercenaries and Allies), it is considered to belong to both its own faction and the host faction for the purposes of Hatred. For example, Black Orcs fielded in a Chorfs army belong to both O&G and Chorfs; a Chaos Giant fielded in a WoC army belongs to both BB and WoC; a Chaos Spawn fielded in a BB army belongs to both WoC and BB.

Note that, unlike Hatred (X), Fear of Elves is a race-based rule. The rule explicitly states that Elves “of any type” cause Fear, making clear that it applies based on a model's race rather than a keyword or faction classification.

Question: Do Characters and Crews benefit from the special rules of its mount and vice versa? If a Character uses an item, spell or ability that specifically affects the caster, does the caster's mount (including chariot crew etc.) benefit from that spell? Can champions use these items?

Unless noted otherwise, the split profile mechanics make any special rule that applies to one element (chariot, character, crew or beasts) apply to the others as well.
Special Rules are shared- both positive and negative.

The same is true for all effects that affect the "model" or "unit", such as Daemonic Vessel.

However, if a spell, item or ability that is not a special rule specifies the caster or character (wearer or bearer) (such as Mantle of Ghorok, or Potion of Fervour) gaining an effect will only affect the character (or champion) itself and not their mount or any components of that split profile model.

Special Rules a character has only apply to the unit if "and any unit they have joined" is mentioned or similar.

Please note that some special rules could cease to apply if a character without a special rule joins a unit or vice versa (e.g. Counter Charge).

Special rules that affect models or weapons do NOT translate from one model to the whole unit or vice versa (a unit with poisoned attacks will not give the character poisoned attacks when joining).

Special rules that only need the majority of models to have the special rule will work (e.g. Reserve Move).

If a character that casted a spell or used an ability "that affects the caster and any unit he has joined" leaves a unit after casting that spell/using the ability, only the caster has the effect, but if he joins another unit, that unit will benefit from that effect too.

if a unit with a character becomes the target of a spell that grants them a Special Rule or Ability, the character can benefit from it while it has joined the unit even if the Special Rule or Ability would prevent them from joining, but will lose it the moment it leaves the unit.

If all the models of the unit are removed as casualties, the unit ceases to exist immediately, and the character loses the Special Rule or Ability.

Anyway, if a character moved or marched before joining a unit, the unit will not count as moved/marched and vice versa.

Question: If the single-use effect of a magic weapon, such as Wollopa’s One Hit Wunda, has not been used or has already been expended, can the wielder choose to use a different mundane weapon instead during combat?
Ruling: No, Wollopa’s One Hit Wunda continues to count as a magical hand weapon even after its single-use effect is expended. Since it remains a magic item, you are not permitted to switch to another mundane weapon in that combat. Remember, general rules for switching weapons between rounds of combat still apply.
Referenced Rules:
Single use magic items CRB 337
Wollopas One Hit wunda RH 43

Turn Order: 4-1 Combat Phase Choose Combat & Determine Who Can Fight
Question: What happens when you charge a unit in the rear with an incomplete rank and kill all models in that rank? Do the models in the "new" rank can attack since they did not step forward nor were killed?
Ruling: No, only those models can attack in their initiative step that were projected into the fighting rank before and weren't killed during prior attacks. To make it easier, you can determine the fighting rank for rear charges at the beginning of the combat, after characters have moved and challenges have been called.
Referenced Rules: Choose Combat & Determine Who can fight CRB 145ff

Question: Can a mounted Character on light chariot (that has to adapt open order formation from its mount) joins a unit that has adopted close order formation?
Ruling: Yes, the rule for mounted character formation ceases to apply as soon as he joins the unit and ceases to be an independent unit - the character will adopt the units formation.

Question: Do other special rules also applies to units that are not yet on the battlefield (or that have left the battlefield for a turn) ? For instance, do they have to roll for Stupidity at the Start of turn sub-phase ? Can they roll for Gaze of the Gods at the Command sub-phase?
Ruling: Units don't count as long as they are not on the battlefield, they don't get to use their special rules.

Turn Order: 4-1 Combat Phase Choose Combat & Determine Who Can Fight
Question: Can models acting on the same Initiative step, rolled one after another, decide to react to changes in the positions of characters, or decide one by one whether to strike at a character or the unit?
Ruling: No, all attacks at the same Initiative step are considered to happen simultaneously. Therefore, changes in the positions of characters, such as a handmaiden retiring after striking, do not affect the resolution of other attacks on that Initiative step. Models attacking on the same Initiative step can still target the character as if she were in her original position.

Question: Are characters without special rule Vanguard, pre-deployment, permitted to Vanguard after joining a unit, post-deployment, with a banner that gives said unit the special rule Vanguard?
Ruling: Yes, if the banner explicitly grants the Vanguard special rule to the entire unit then the character can Vanguard. However, the GW FAQ clarifies that a character does not gain Vanguard if it joins a unit that has the rule only in its profile. This distinction arises because Vanguard in a unit’s profile does not automatically extend to joined characters unless specifically stated by an upgrade, like a banner, that applies to the entire unit.

Question: Can a cannonball hit a character, which has joined a unit with 5 or more rank and file models?
Ruling: Yes, since a cannon ball hits a model and not the unit, the character is hit (targeted by an attack that allows a specific model within the unit to be targeted). If there are 5 or more rank and file models that character is allowed to make a Look Out, Sir! - roll. This also applies to unit champions or special models within units.
Referenced Rules:
Cannon Fire CRB 226
Characters & Shooting CRB 209

Question: If a unit decides to rearrange its ranks during a reform maneuver, is it limited to 5 models similar to redress the ranks?
Ruling: No, but no model is allowed to move further than double its movement characteristic during a reform.

Question: There are a some items, which have restrictions for "characters" regarding the acess or the use of these items. Can unit champions with access to magic items buy or use these items?
Ruling: If the type of character is not specified further (for example "beastmen chieftain only or necromancer only"), champions are allowed to take and use these items with the same restrictions. If the items have any restrictions that apply generally to Characters, those restrictions also apply to non-Characters models that can take the items.

Question: What happens when a unit with Random Movement makes a Pursuit, Overrun, Flee, Fall Back in Good Order, or conducts similar movements?
Ruling: Only use Random Movement during the Compulsory Movement phase or any movement based on the unit's Movement characteristic. For all other movement types (e.g., FBIGO, fleeing, pursuing etc.), follow the rules for the relevant move type as stated in the rulebook, including distance rolls.

Question: What are the size restrictions for player-created terrain, such as the forest from Woodland Ambush or the Herdstone? Can these be asymmetrical, hollow, or other unusual shapes?
Ruling: For player-created forests, they must be between 3" at their narrowest and 9" at their widest point, which limits most unusual shapes. The Herdstone must be no more than 6" at its widest point, but has no minimum size or limits on unusual shapes. However, while there is no specific limitation in the rules, it is recommend that players check with the TO of their event before entering a tournament with a terrain piece that has a very unusual shape (especially if the shape is designed to provide a specific competitive advantage, such as a hollow herdstone) as it is common for TOs to disallow the use of these irregular designs.

Question: Can a character that attempts to use an ability that requires a leadership test use the 'hold your ground' ability of an undead battle standard bearer to re-roll this test?
Ruling: Yes

Turn Order: 4-1 Combat Phase Choose Combat & Determine Who Can Fight
Question: For monster handlers, is the D6 roll to check whether a wound removes a handler or makes the monster lose a wound only during combat, or for any unsaved wounds?
Ruling: The roll occurs for any unsaved wounds, since the last phrase of the paragraph is also not related only to combat. The "in combat" only applies to the first phrase.

Question: Which set of rules must be used for a character riding a behemoth with Howdah?
Ruling: Split profile (chariot mount), because Howdah references Split profile (chariots)

Question: Can Skaven Master assassins and Dark Elves Khainite assassins be hidden in a unit that is not deployed at the start of the game (for instance ambushers)?
Ruling: Yes

Question: When is decided the unit where Skaven Master assassins and Dark Elves Khainite assassins are hidden ?
Ruling: When deploying characters

Turn Order: 4-1 Combat Phase Choose Combat & Determine Who Can Fight
Question: Spectral Doppelganger - Which weapon can a model use for the spell? When are the hits of a Strike Last Weapon resolved? What happens if the caster dies before the attacks are resolved after he made the cast?
Ruling: Any melee weapon the model carries can be used, magical or not. For a Strike Last weapon, the attacks are resolved at Initiative 1, unmodified as the spell gives you a initiative value. If the caster dies before the attacks are made, the attacks will be resolved at I1.

Question: What happens when a unit charges a unit and has no other choice but to charge in a way that a third (opponent) unit is within 1" of the charging unit
Ruling: Since charge moves are conducted in the movement phase, the 1" rule comes to use and the units have to be nudged 1" away

Turn Order: 4-1 Combat Phase Choose Combat & Determine Who Can Fight
Question: Is a champion removed as a casualty when he is in a challenge and the whole unit is removed as a casualty, including an unsaved wound for the champion?
Ruling: Yes, no Rule in champions ( 199) prevents the champion from being removed

Question: Can a unit start / declare a march after it already made maneuver that you normally cannot use whilst marching?
Ruling: No it cannot, a unit either marches or does not march.

Question: Do you have to announce the use of your general’s leadership before a break or leadership test or after the test is done?
Ruling: Since the sequence for break tests clearly states rolling first and then comparing and checking later, you can roll first and then use Inspiring Presence or not, depending on the dice roll. For leadership tests, Inspiring Presence is optional too, since under Inspiring Presence "can” is stated.

Question: Can a Salamander Pack or a similar unit that is both War beasts and Regular infantry, benefit from Inspiring Presence ?
Ruling: No, the War Beast Troop Type gives the unit the undisciplined special rule

Question: Can units with the special rule dragged along be drawn by units with the special rule Fly (X)?
Ruling: Yes, use the movement distance in the brackets of Fly(X) but move the model dragged along on the ground - not using fly movement.

Turn Order: 4-1 Combat Phase Choose Combat & Determine Who Can Fight
Question: Does the multiple wounds (X) special rule work against war machine (crews) in combat?
Ruling: The crew is a single profile that loses attacks as it loses wounds. Multiple wounds works against it.

Turn Order: 4-1 Combat Phase Choose Combat & Determine Who Can Fight
Question: Motley Crew: When do you determine which casualties are removed in combat / what the majority of models is?
Ruling: Check at the beginning of each initiative step when attacks are made. Check the majority of models of both fighting ranks, first and second, for the majority of models and use their armour save. Then for all unsaved wounds, remove casualties among those which have a majority. Apply the principles of casualty removal (first rank eligible to fight first, then second, then support attacks, then stepping forward) only among the models who have a majority. This can lead to the case that models from the second fighting rank are removed before models in the first fighting rank. Models that do not belong the the majority of the fighting rank are only removed after all models of the unit that do belong to the majority of the fighting rank for each initiative step. Note that a champion that choses a wholly different weapon counts as a separate pool. In case of a tie, the controlling player decides which armour save to use and which models to remove (you have to remove the models of which you use the armour save).

Question: What happens when a unit that gives ground cannot move more than 1" and will be within 1" of a unit it is in combat with, be it because of terrain or other units?
Ruling: Since giving ground is not possible, the units remain locked in combat, but all units move as far as possible and remain locked at the new position (see GW FAQ).

Question: Can a Champion that is not on the table (because he is in Ambush, or hold back as Reserves) Challenge or accept the Challenge of a Warrior Duel ?
Ruling: Yes, nothing in the wording of the rule implies that the Champion's Unit of the Marauder or their opponent have to be actually on the battlefield to fight in the Warrior Duel.

Turn Order: 4-1 Combat Phase Choose Combat & Determine Who Can Fight
Question: Does a unit gain the benefit of a defended Low linear obstacle when the charging unit ends the charge move on top of the LLO in base contact to the unit or at a part of the unit where there is no LLO
Ruling: The last sentence only mentions Fly (X) as an exception, so a charging unit always suffers the disordered charge but only loses impact hits and stomp attacks and full attacks if it has no base contact/for models without base contact

Question: If a spell or ability states “all units within y may” or “all units within y gain an effect”, what happens if a unit moves outside of Y or the caster moves?
Ruling: All units that are within Y may benefit from that effect, given they are within Y at the time they want to use the effect (aka the effect moves with the caster for the whole duration of X).
Referenced Rules: Hellish Vigour Khsar's Incantation of the Desert Wind

Question: Can a Skink character join a Salamander Pack, a skirmisher unit which has both Regular infantry and War beast troop sub-types ?
Ruling: No, since skink characters do not have both regular infantry and the war beast troop type.

Question: Can you decide to alter the charge path of a charging unit to avoid discarding the higher dice to make your charge successful, if you would instead fail the charge because of the terrain (by rolling a 1 and a 6 on the charge roll for instance, in addition to -1 M)?
Ruling: Yes. You define the path taken by the unit after rolling the dice (it's already the case for wheeling to maximise contact) because you must move by the shortest route possible to reach the charge target. Make charges happen if possible.

Question: Does the free wheel to align count in the charge move distance for the purpose of rules like Furious Charge and Impact Hits (reminder: When a unit wheels, every model counts as having moved as far as the outside model. Page 124)?
Ruling: The free Wheel takes place after making contact. It is separated from the charge move, both for placement and initiative.
Referenced Rules:
Aligning to the Enemy CRB 126
Who Strikes first? CRB 146

Question: How many demonic gifts can a demon of chaos character buy? Does a character equipped with a Daemonic Locus count as a Battle Standard Bearer?
Ruling: Since there are no categories for the demonic gifts mentioned as in the rulebook for magic items, a character can buy as many different gifts as his point limit allows. Demonic gifts without an asterik can only be taken once per army. The character with Daemonic Locus is a BSB in all respects, in addition to having the Daemonic Locus special rule and for characters, only a demonic locus can buy a single icon.

Question: Can a unit with random movement move into contact with a unit that was not "at least partly in its front arc" as long as it fulfills all criteria for charging (single wheel etc.) stated on 126 (see GW FAQ)? For example, an enemy unit that is behind the unit with random movement but reachable with a single wheel?
Ruling: Yes, you don't need LoS or the enemy unit to be in your front arc since you do not declare the charge. As long as you fulfill the charge criteria (shortest route, only one wheel etc.), that is a perfectly acceptable "move into contact".

Turn Order: 2-1 Movement Phase Declare Charges and Charge Reaction
Question: Can you use counter charge against a redirected charge?
Ruling: No, only hold or flee are possible against a redirected charge.

Turn Order: 2-1 Movement Phase Declare Charges and Charge Reaction
Question: If I am redirecting a charge and the new target was already a charged target by another unit, can this new target declare to Flee now if it already declared to Hold against its initial charging enemycharge against a redirected charge?
Ruling: Yes, the redirected charge calls to a new reaction but the only choices are Hold and Flee. The soldiers see the new enemy coming and it can change their initial decision.

Question: Give Ground : A unit giving ground stops moving immediately should it come into contact with another unit or terrain. Which type of terrain is meant here?
Ruling: Only physical terrain features that are not open ground, meaning no hills and no vortexes. Note that this also affects units already in terrain prior to the give ground move, meaning that a unit already in terrain can't give ground and instead does not move

Question: Do you have to be eligible for a wizardly dispell attempt to use arcane "instead of a (wizardly) dispell items"?
Ruling: Yes, the GW FAQ to Glowing Green Amulet is only about this specific item

Question: What happens if a unit makes contact with another unit not being the charge target during the free wheel of alignement?
Ruling: If it was clear at the time of the charge declaration that the projected charge will end like this and you will hit the second unit during alignment, no matter the charge roll, you have to declare a charge against both units. If there is a slight possibility to avoid this situation, the unit should try and wheel around that unit. If it is impossible to avoid the contact in any case with the given charge roll result (but would have been with a better charge roll result), the charging unit conducts an accidental contact during a charge and may chose to either halt the charge (leading to a disordered charge with most likely only 1 model in base contact against the original charge target) or to continue (leading to a disordered charge with both units, in which the accidental contacted units might try to align). If the unit continues into a fleeing unit, the fleeing unit is destroyed and the charging unit's movement comes to an end. The charged unit wheels to align if necessary, in which case the charging unit makes a disordered charge.
Referenced Rules: Accidental Contact during a Charge CRB 131

Question: If you declare a charge against multiple units, is that charge a failed charge if you contact one of the units only with the free wheel from aligning?
Ruling: No, this is still a valid charge.
Referenced Rules:
Multiple Charge Targets CRB 130
Accidental Contact during a Charge CRB 131

Question: Some Options (Equipment) confer Special Rules to Characters. Do Mounts also benefit from these special rules if they affect the Armour Save? Can this special rule be used to overcome a max. armour save?
Ruling: Yes, these special rules affect also the mount. No, the max. Armour Save (3+) for Monsters, Chariots and War Machines is unaffected by this and will cap the Armour Save.
Referenced Rules:
Arcane Journal High Elves Lions Cloak
Dark Elves Sea Dragon Cloak

Question: Can you cast assailment spells during a warriors duel ("like in a challenge")? Assailment spells are cast in every "combat phase", the warriors duel only states that there "rounds of combat"
Ruling: Yes, rounds of combat are conducted in the combat phase, so its possible

Question: Goad Beast: During the Command sub-phase of their turn, this character may goad a single friendly model whose troop type is ‘monster’ and that is within their Command range (including their own mount). Until the end of this turn, that model gains a +D3 modifier to its Attacks characteristic (to a maximum of 10). Does this also affect the rider?
Ruling: No, only the mount, see 'including their own mount' - see Split Profile (monster mount) - The character and mount each use their own Weapon Skill, Ballistic Skill, Strength, Initiative and Attacks characteristics,

Question: If a unit marches through difficult terrain, how is the movement calculated?
Ruling: 2(M-1) - Reduce the movement characteristic by one, then double it.

Question: Are hits suffered by miscast magical attacks?
Ruling: Yes, given the nature of spellcasting, they are magical attacks

Question: When calculating how many models can shoot using Volley Fire, when do you round?
Ruling: You round after calculating the models in each rank. Example: For a unit that is 5 models wide and 5 ranks deep on level ground, 5 from the first rank, 3 each from the second (5/2=2.5, rounded to 3), third, fourth, and fifth ranks can shoot. In total, 17 models will shoot.

Turn Order: 4-1 Combat Phase Choose Combat & Determine Who Can Fight
Question: When a model steps forward during a combat, then the unit overruns into a new and unresolved combat, does the model get to make attacks?
Ruling: No. A model may not make attacks during the same phase in which it stepped forward.

Question: Can I contact (and so charge) an enemy unit if I already have redirected the charge of this unit this turn?
Ruling: Yes, the unit count as redirecting, but it has not redirected.
Referenced Rules: Accidental Contact During A Charge CRB 131

Question: Can a unit with Random movement reform when restraining from pursuing or following up, when rallying (including fall back in good order) or after destroying a fleeing enemy unit ?
Ruling: Yes, the restriction on not being able to perform manoeuvres only applies when moving with their Random Movement characteristic.

Question: What is happening when a model with random movement is put in base contact with a fleeing unit ? Does the unit flees again or is it destroyed ?
Ruling: The unit is destroyed - no charge reaction is given when being contacted by a unit with random movement.

Question: How do you deteremine cover if a model can see multiple arcs of an opponent unit?
Ruling: Check all line of sights from the shooting model to all models of the target unit, ignoring the lines which cross over models of the target unit. Models of the target unit you cannot see because of other models of that unit are ignored. Apply then the rules for cover, depending on how much of the unit is obscured. Note that according to GW FAQ, Woods give cover even without LOS crossing over them, as long as more than half of the target unit is within the Wood.

Question: Can a character move more than twice its movement to use 'Move through the ranks' or when he joins a unit to reach the front rank?
Ruling: Yes. Since the fighting rank is at a fixed location, he is obliged to move that distance to get to the fighting rank. The only times when a character inside of a unit is subject to this (besides normal maneuvering/moving) is Reform and Redress the ranks.

Question: How many wailing dirges does a Mortis engine have?
Ruling: You only do one wailing dirge attack for the whole mortis engine.

Question: Does a unit partially on a hill gets cover for models, for which the LoS is obstructed by the hill?
Ruling: Yes. (RAW)

Question: Does a unit gets cover, when the LoS that checks cover is partially obstructed by a unit closer to the center of a hill?
Ruling: Yes
Referenced Rules:
GW FAQ
Vantage Point CRB 271
Beyond the Crest CRB 271

Question: If a unit wants to shoot at units on a hill - do units that are on the same hill and are further from the center than the target unit block line of sight for the shooting unit?
Ruling: No, since they can see you over that unit, you can see them too - the rules for being closer to the center of the hill works both ways, imagine the unit closer to the center being higher elevated.
Referenced Rules:
GW FAQ
Vantage Point CRB 271
Beyond the Crest CRB 271

Question: Can you see a unit that is only partially on a hill and can you see a model that is only partially on a hill?
Ruling: Yes, given no other unit obstructs that LoS. Treat models and units partially on a hill as they were on the ground, but the hill itself blocks no line of sight to those models that are partially on the hill.
Referenced Rules:
GW FAQ
Vantage Point CRB 271
Beyond the Crest CRB 271

Question: Does a wizarding hat allow a character to buy arcane items? If the Character was a Wizard before and buys an arcane item. Does the Arcane Item affect spellcasting and spell generation of this model?
Ruling: No, see GW FAQ. As explained in the GW FAQ, the wearer is not actually a Wizard, but instead the Hat is the wizard. Since the hat is not affected by armour the bearer wears, it is also not affected by arcane items.

Question:
How do "laser beam" spells and attacks such as Gaze of Gork, Burning Gaze and Lightning Strike (from the Warp Lightning Canon) work?

When the game rules calls for using a line (to determine models hit from "laser beams" special rules such as Gaze of Gork, or by models with the Cannon Fire special rule, or for the secondary objective Domination), what is the thickness of the line? Can it ever touch two models in a formed up unit at the same time over the same point, given that these models touch?
Ruling:
Once the spell is cast, choose a direction, then determine the distance of the line. This line does not require a target and therefore ignores all targeting rules, i.e. it can be drawn over LoS-blocking terrain, hit models in combat, lone characters, fanatics, and models the caster doesn't have LoS to.

In geometry, a straight line is an infinitely long object with no width, depth, or curvature. Although models in a formed up unit are touching edge-to-edge, they do not share a space, and since the line has no width, there is no point on the line that can be over two models simultaneously.
Practically, this means that a laser beam can only be crossing a single model at any given point, and so can never be shot exactly alongside the line where two files (or ranks) of a formed up units touch in order to hit both, or exactly over the point where the corners of 4 bases are touching in order to hit all 4.
The path of a cannonball follows the same principles, with the added restriction of only being able to hit a single model per rank under the path when firing in the unit's front arc, or per file when firing in the unit's flank.
Finally, this means that if a unit straddles over two quarters for Domination, it is not possible to position it so that all of its models are wholly within one quarter or the other.
Referenced Rules:
Gaze of Gork
Burning Gaze
Lightning Strike
Warplightning Cannon

Question: Can characters with the ambush special rule join a unit with ambush pre-placement?
Ruling: Yes they can, use the rules for Characters and Reserves - announce each turn before rolling any dices

Question: Do frenzied (or impetuous) units always have to use Swiftstride or Fly when charging
Ruling: Yes, see GW FAQ they always will use special rules that benefit their charge.

Question: How do Skirmishers conduct a flee move or Give Ground? What happens when they flee through units?
Ruling:
If in Skirmish Formation (not formed up), determine center-to-center, then flee  with all models parallel in this direction without pivoting the unit. Give Ground the same way, stopping the whole unit if at least one model encounters an obstacle.

If any model in the skirmish unit moves through another unit, then all models continue moving in the same direction until they are no longer within 1" of an enemy or overlapping a friendly unit, taking peril tests as normal.

If models flee through units, move the whole unit the same distance.  If the unit encounters an impassable terrain piece, each model moves as close as possible along that terrain piece and returns then to the original flee path

During Flee or Give Ground, if at least one model moves off the board, the whole unit is destroyed.

Question: If a unit with the Fly (X) special rule declares and makes a charge, when do you have to declare which Movement characteristic (Fly or normal) the unit will use?
Ruling: Declare which movement will be used as the unit declares the charge

Question: Multiple Charges into Skirmishers: What happens if you get a different side presented after forming up of the Skirmishers against the first Unit?
Ruling: Skirmishers as GW FAQ do not have arcs, just move in the side presented to you after forming up.

Question: Multiple Charges into Skirmishers: What happens if the formed up side towards your unit is "full" so you cannot make contact with that side?
Ruling: Go to the side of that "arc"("flank" - remember, no arcs), but you have to able to get there with only 1 wheel, else you fail the charge

Question: Multiple Charges into Skirmishers: What happens if you can go straight forward in but also you can maximize if you go into another side of the unit?
Ruling: Charge to the side, maximizing has priority, but remember that you are only allowed to do one wheel, sometimes you will be able to do this, while sometimes you have to priorize charging over maximizing - use the principles of charging, priorizing top to bottom.

Question: Can characters without the ambush special rule join a unit with ambush pre-placement?
Ruling: No

Question: Can you drill a unit that is part of multiple units charging an unit if the unit with drilled is blocked on both sides by units that charge along of that unit?
Ruling: No, Drilled takes place before the charge move and the units are considered to move simultaneously. Would the units charge different targets, the active player could first move the blocking units away and drill then. With multiple units charging the same target, this is not possible.
Referenced Rules:
Drilled CRB 167
Multiple Charging Units CRB 130

Question: Can a unit that is charging make use of the Drilled special rule in a way that causes accidental contact during a charge or that results in a charge against multiple targets?
Ruling: No, unless the unit is in marching column and the minimum widt requested to leave the marching column already causes accidental / a multiple target charge. In that case the unit is allowed to Redress the ranks to be able to charge and conduct a multiple charge against other targets, but only against those needed to actually conduct the charge.
Referenced Rules:
Multiple Charge Targets CRB 130
Accidental Contact During a Charge CRB 131

Question: If a Doom Diver fires indirectly, do you allow for a -d3 instead of the ballistic skill and then another d3 directional correction?
Ruling: Yes, the second part of the Doom Diver Rule referes to the indirect fire part of the bombardment rule of 225, so the first part gets applied too.

Question: If a unit is not listed in the army list composition section of "characters", but one of its subtype is "character", does it counts for the 3 minimum non-character units needed for army composition? (not including ones with troop type swarm/war beastes/war machine)?
Ruling: No, they are character units.

Turn Order: 4-1 Combat Phase Choose Combat & Determine Who Can Fight
Question: Can a champion move through the ranks?
Ruling: No, only non-champion characters are allowed to do so.

Turn Order: 4-1 Combat Phase Choose Combat & Determine Who Can Fight
Question: When moving through the ranks to join the fighting rank, can a character choose its position?
Ruling: A character can freely choose any position in the fighting rank, regardless of base contact or not.

Question: How do you flee along an impassable terrain? If a fleeing unit reaches impassable terrain, how does it move?
Ruling:
First, begin to flee as normal.

If the flee move would cause the unit to contact impassable terrain, it must pivot around its centre as soon as it is possible for the unit’s flank to be flush against the terrain feature, while facing the direction which will allow it to resume its flee move along its initial flee path as directly as possible. The unit will continue to flee along the side of the impassable terrain until it is able to pivot again around the feature's corner, and move along the next side of the feature (this might need to be done multiple times in case of a non-square feature, or multiple impassable features), until its centre is back on top of the initial direction of flight, at which point the unit will pivot in order to resume fleeing in its initial direction.

In the case where the unit is too close to pivot its flank against the impassable feature (this is often the case for very wide units, even if they are not backed against the feature), it must first pivot around its centre while facing the direction which will allow it to resume the unit’s flee move along its initial flee path as directly as possible. It then moves forward (taking peril tests as required), until pivoting with the unit’s flank against the feature is possible, then follow the procedure described above.

Question: If I have multiple characters' base does not fit neatly (non-fitting bases) can they go on the same side?
Ruling: The characters join the front of the unit and are placed on either the left or right flank, as shown in Figure (need reference from rules). Only one such character can be placed on each flank of the unit. For determining marching column or combat order, these models are ignored.

Question: Does a champion count for the bretonnia exiles blessing if slain in a challenge - or can a champion even get a blessing of the lady if he kills a character or champion in a challenge?
Ruling: No, only non-champion characters are counting for this and a champion cannot get the blessing separately from the unit

Question: Can a champion shoot magic missiles (from bound spells or wizarding hat or if he is a wizard) into another target than his unit?
Ruling: Yes, the wording for characters on 209 is the same as for champions on 199. This heavily implies that the exemption also counts for champions.
Referenced Rules:
Characters and Shooting CRB 209
Champions CRB 199

Question: Can characters shoot multiple magic missiles per turn into different targets? A lone character would still be treated as a unit and therefore has to target the same unit?
Ruling: Yes he can, the exemption for magic missiles on 209 is to be applied - a character can divide his magic missiles into different targets, chosing targets when each spell is cast.

Question: Do models with the fly (x) rule suffer a -1 movement penalty and have to use the lowest of 2d6 when charging while starting their movement in terrain.
Ruling: Yes, models with fly (x) always begin their movement on the ground, and any unit that start their movement in terrain suffers its effects.

Question: With the new GW FAQ about taking wheeling into account for allowing charges, can you declare charges with Swiftstride if the opponent is within M+9 but with wheel M+12?
Ruling: The opponent unit has to be both within M+9 maximum charge range and it has to be possible to conduct the charge with M+9 including the wheels.

Question: How is a unit of skirmishers moved by the spell Travel Mystical Pathway?
Ruling: Draw a 12" radius around the whole unit. Each model can be replaced anywhere within that radius in coherency, and at least 6" away from any enemy unit.

Question: Can you cast a Remains in Play spell, that is already casted?
Ruling: Yes. While the rulebook says no, GW FAQ clarifies that the spell can be attempted to cast, but the current active spell is ended on the attempt.

Question: When two units are in combat with the same facing of an enemy unit that flees from combat, how is the pursuit resolved? Do the units block each other when moving toward or pivoting to face the fleeing enemy?
Ruling: Each pursuit happens sequentially, with the controlling player choosing their order. Pivot moves always ignore the presence of other units and terrain. When the first unit makes its pursuit, it may end overlapping with another friendly unit that was part of that combat (even though this is normally now allowed); and may move through those units until the first units move is complete. The other units do ignore the other units when making its own pivot aswell, but their move will often be blocked by the unit that has moved first. If the unit can only partly pivot and will overlap after pivot with the unit that has moved first, it pivots instead as far as it is able toward the fleeing enemy and does not move further.

Question: If Galrauch fails a leadership test, when does the condition end?
Ruling: Until the start of his next turn, since he has to test again

Turn Order: 2-1 Movement Phase Declare Charges and Charge Reaction
Question: Should all effects that impact stand and shoot apply to all rules that utilize it as a function such as fire and flee?
Ruling: Yes, errata all rules that impact stand and shoot to apply to any rule that uses it as part of its functions (Banner of Chalons, Quick Shot)

Stand & Shoot CRB 120
Fire & Flee CRB 169

Question: In order to overrun, a unit must destroy its enemy completely. Which "enemies" are meant by this?
Ruling: This refers to all enemy units the unit is engaged in combat with—specifically, those in base contact. In combats involving multiple units, even if the enemy units in direct base contact are wiped out, the unit remains part of the combat until end of turn. Combat results still factor in this unit, and it must undergo any required break tests and suffer all consequences.

Question: How are multiple Hits with the Multiple Wounds (X) special rule resolved against a unit with multiple Multiple Wound models? How do situations work where hits are inflicted on certain models (Cannons etc.)
Ruling:
Resolve attacks against the models that are hit in specific cases like cannons, or allocated attacks against champions or against the unit if the unit is attacked. This means, use the  weapon skill, toughness, armour and ward saves accordingly.

Unsaved wounds are then applied one after another to the unit, except in the case of champions being hit, which have their own conditions under which they are hit separately, including cannons (which can hit the champion separately). Page 102 and GW FAQ tell us to start with wounds that inflict Killing Blow, followed by Multiple Wound (X) wounds, and finally ending with single wound attacks. For wounds on the unit, Allocate these wounds starting with the model that is already wounded (ignore the champion if he is wounded already).

Question: How do you follow up? And what happens if, while performing the follow up move towards a unit that Gives Ground, the unit would contact instead another enemy unit that was not in the combat? Is it accidental contact or should movement stop at 1" from the unit that would be contacted?
Ruling: To conduct a follow up move, do the opposite of give ground: move directly towards the enemy unit that gave ground, without turning, pivoting or otherwise changing its facing in any way until you make contact or until you stop because of contact with an impassable terrain or friendly unit. If you contact another enemy unit, this is accidental contact (pg. 131). if the enemy unit is contacted in the rear or flank, or if it is already in combat, nudge that unit and any units it is in combat with) aside and conduct the follow up move. If the enemy unit is contacted in its front, it can chose to accept the combat, effectively stopping the follow up move or give ground to avoid it.
Referenced Rules:
Accidental Contact CRB 130
Follow Up CRB 156

Question: Can you decide not to use Lore Familiar, even if the wizard bought the item?
Ruling: If the Wizard opts not to do it they don’t get any spells at all RAW

Turn Order: 3-3 Shooting Phase Roll to Wound & Make Armour Saves

Question: Regarding the Challenges & Mounts Change - how do you determine which attacks are lost?
Ruling: If one participant of the challenge is slain in one initiative step, all attacks with a lower initiative in this combat are lost and will not be conducted. You can only score overkill from attacks of the same initiative of the step in which the participant is slain.

Turn Order: 2-1 Movement Phase Declare Charges and Charge Reaction
Question: Can you still Counter Charge on turn 1 after a Vanguard move?

Question: Spider Banner: Can the unit wound automatically?
Ruling: No they can't, they just get Poison on natural 5+ instead of 6 if they already had poison before.

Question: Big Smartz: If a unit failed a stupidity test but succeeds another one before my next start of turn sub-phase, is the unit still stupid ?: Can the unit wound automatically?
Ruling: No, a stupid unit ceases to be stupid if it succeeds a stupidity test.

Question: What happens when a model that belongs to a unit of single wound models has multiple hits allocated specifically to this model? (for example Tree Whack)
Ruling: If the model and not the unit is hit, the model is killed, but wounds from additional hits do not spill over to other models

Question: How do you determine in which arc of a charge target a single model is?
Ruling: Only check the front edge of the model - if the majority of the front edge of a model is in one arc, then charge this arc. If you cannot come to an agreement with your opponent, charge the arc which offers the lower combat resolution

Turn Order: 4-1 Combat Phase Choose Combat & Determine Who Can Fight
Question: Do one-handed magic weapons, which do not count as any other weapon type, qualify for the Parry special rule of Infantry?
Ruling: Only if the weapon is specifically stated to be or count as hand weapon (right now that is only the wollopa one hit wounda after use)

Turn Order: 4-1 Combat Phase Choose Combat & Determine Who Can Fight
Question: Do Parry (from Infantry) and Parry (Guardians of Talsyn) stack?
Ruling: Yes, but note that the normal Parry will only be granted if fighting with a hand weapon, not with an Asrai Spear

Question: How do the Arrows of Isha and the Seafarer Bow interact?
Ruling: You take the best of the two profiles of Bow. This effectively gives Bow of the Seafarer with Arrows of Isha the profile; AP-3 AB(1)."

Turn Order: 4-1 Combat Phase Choose Combat & Determine Who Can Fight
Question: If a unit A is engaged with two units B and C, one (B) of which is a single character in a challenge, the rules say that all models of the first unit A which normally must attack the character B due to closeness instead are allowed to attack the other unit C. How does this work with fighting ranks and "full attacks"?
Ruling: Since "the unit" is specified in the FAQ about fighting ranks, only the models within M" of Unit C can attack that unit. Please note that these models only get to make 1 A, regardless if they are in base contact with B or not.

Question: Does the change in Regeneration mean that i can use a Regeneration save for any case a model loses a wound, even if just losing a wound is stated? E.g. can you attempt a Regeneration save against Peril Tests, Deamonic Instability, Dangerous Terrain and similar cases?
Ruling: Yes, as long that it is not mentioned that regeneration saves are not permitted against these attacks. Please note that due to the old wording of regeneration, Killing Blow, Monster Slayer and similar wordings do NOT allow regeneration saves to be made against the wounds lost with these special rules.

Turn Order: 4-1 Combat Phase Choose Combat & Determine Who Can Fight
Question: Does the new FAQ entry of the Fighting Rank mean that all ranks and files which have only one model in contact with opponent models count as Fighting Ranks?
Ruling: When two opposing units are engaged in combat, only one row of models—the rank or file that is both in base contact and aligned (or almost in disordered charges) to the enemy’s engaged row—is considered the fighting rank. Other ranks or files that merely contain a single model in contact do not count as fighting ranks. Exceptions to this rule apply only to units in Lance Formation, Skirmishers, and Infantry (which has two fighting ranks in some cases), which may have different fighting rank rules.

Question: How would situations resolved where a character without the First Charge rule joins a unit that has it and vice versa?
Ruling: As long as one model with the rule First Charge is performing its first charge of the game within a unit, the special rule is used and counts as being used for all models that participated in that charge and have the First Charge special rule in that unit

Question: Do i have to maximize with a lance charging another unit?
Ruling: No, since the lance automatically is in base contact, you don't have to maximize at all - just charge the closest way in.

Turn Order: 4-1 Combat Phase Choose Combat & Determine Who Can Fight
Question: If one of the participants of a challenge is defending a Low linear obstacle, are both characters treated as being in base to base contact?
Ruling: No, still treat them as having the LLO between them - no Impact or Stomp Attacks.

Question: Can you do a second bombing run with the Sky Lantern or Gyrocopter or do a second Wake of Fire Attack with the Flamespyre Phoenix and similar attacks which are triggered just by moving close or over the opponent when moving with Arcane Urgency or the Rune of Haste and Urgency?
Ruling: Yes, given the ability does not have a restriction regarding the number (once per remaining move phase or similar) which it can be used per turn or in total.

Question: Can a Dwarf with a weapon that has Weapon runes inscribed on it use Parry?
Ruling: As long as the weapon is a hand weapon.

Question: What happens if a character joins a single rank unit?
Ruling: The character goes to the first rank, displacing one model to a newly formed second rank, as described under Positioning Characters.

Question: With the new ruling on shooting at characters that have joined a unit with different troop type, how do you process that shooting?
Ruling: The character is targeted instead of the unit. All Line of Sight and Range are measured towards the character. Note that the unit is not able to use evasive or similar special rules and the character cannot be protected by 'Lone character' rules.

Turn Order: 4-1 Combat Phase Choose Combat & Determine Who Can Fight
Question: How do you calculate the correct armour save if you have Parry, other modifiers, and Armour Piercing?
Ruling: Parry cannot improve your armour save beyond a 3+ value. This means that when calculating the base armour save (before any roll modifiers), Parry will cap the result at 3+ if not improved by other means. However, if the unit is affected by a rule that modifies the armour save value itself (e.g. Plague of Rust), you can balance positive and negative modifiers against each other. For example Rune of Oath & Steel. Note that modifiers to the armour save roll—like Armour Piercing, Totem of Rust, etc.—do not interact with this cap and leave it at 3+. They apply after the save value is determined, and reduce the final roll needed for success.

Turn Order: 4-1 Combat Phase Choose Combat & Determine Who Can Fight
Question: If an infantry model that has an 2+ Armour Save (without parry), fights with hand weapon and shield - does it have to use parry and only has a 3+ Asv as the consequence?
Ruling: While the model has to use parry, parry only improves the armour save - therefore, the model retains its 2+ Asv. Note that you cannot use the parry bonus to get to a 2+ Armour Save by any means.

Question: Can you take a virtue of the duty or ideal even if that means that your general has not the highest Ld in your army?
Ruling: Yes, only the BSB is mentioned in GWs FAQ on the highest leadership. This also means in your army you can include mercenaries or other characters that are not able to be the general with a higher leadership than your general.

Question: Ethereal treats all terrain as open ground, and Grinding Wheels does the same for Low Lineae Obstacles. How does this interact with units that are defending a LLO?
Ruling: Because the charge is a move, these units fully ignore the LLO and will move on top of it. For all purposes, units with these rules ignore defended LLO rules.

Question: How do you charge a unit behind a defended Low linear obstacle?
Ruling: Charge the LLO and align towards the LLO instead of the unit. Note that you have to charge the LLO in a way that at least one model of the charging unit is in the front arc of the defending unit, else the charge is considered to be a failed charge. Maximise in a way that as many models as possible are within M" of each other. Also remember that a Lance blunts if charging a unit behind a LLO because it is considered to have conducted a disordered charge.

Question: How do abilities like Gnashing Maws (gigantic spawn of chaos) interact with regeneration? What about effects that trigger when a model loses its last wound, such as Timmm-berr!, Grail Pendant or Explosive Demise (warpfire dragon)?
Ruling: Regeneration is no longer a save, so a wound from Gnashing Maws counts as an unsaved wound regardless of whether regeneration is successful. Effects that require a model to lose its last wound will only trigger if the model actually loses its last wound after any regeneration saves attempted.

Question: Can an engineer in combat use a pigeon bomb?
Ruling: No because this is "instead of shooting normally", so the engineer needs to be able to shoot

Question: Given the FAQ for Open Orders Quick Turn - does this apply to Lumbering aswell?
Ruling: Only Quick Turn is mentioned, Lumbering can still be used outside of sequence

Question: When items or abilites do enhance the Range of a Spell, do they also enhance the range of spell effects that are explained in the spells' description?
Ruling: Only the range for targeting units is extended, so spell effects are not increased. In Detail: For Vortex Spells, the range of effect is not enhanced, only the range for template placement. For Conveyance pells, the target range is increased but not the range of replacement (Travel Mystical Pathways, Infernal Gateway). For Spells with Self range, nothing is increased. For Gaze of Gork, the Range is extended.

Question: Can characters that joined a unit of the same troop type be targeted by enemy shooting if there are fewer than five rank and file models (of the same troop type) in the unit they have joined?
Ruling: No, the only change that GW's errata makes is to prevent characters of different types from receiving the protection enjoyed by same-type characters in units. When there are fewer than five rank and file models in a unit, the second paragraph of "Enemy Shooting" in the errata gives you instructions of how such characters can be hit when their units aren't of sufficient size.

Question: Stupidity: What happens if a stupid unit does fbigo or rallies, can it reform upon a rally? What happens if the unit gives ground?
Ruling: The unit does not give ground and cannot reform when rallying, changing face or use similar abilities (drilled, lumbering etc.). You cannot you use infernal gateway or travel mystical pathway on these units, a move is a move (except obligatory moves, which can be done)

Question: Can conveyance spells be cast on units or targets who already moved during that Movement Phase, including charging, fleeing or moving during the compulsory moves?
Ruling: Yes. Unless otherwise specified in the spell's description, such spells can be cast on any valid friendly unit, respecting the normal criteria for choosing a target (i.e. within the caster's vision arc and range, not engaged in combat). Specific constraints and/or allowances may be defined in the spell's description, e.g. regarding the target unit/character's movement before and/or after the spell, or whether it is fleeing or engaged in combat.

Question: Skirmishers can defend a Low Linear Obstacle (LLO) by "moving as many models as possible into base contact with it." What exactly does this mean?
Ruling: In order to defend a LLO, a skirmish unit must move as many models as can reach the LLO within a single movement, and have at least one model in the unit end its move with one side of its base fully in contact with the long edge of the LLO. When a charge is declared against the defending skirmish unit, the enemy unit will move as normal for charging a skirmish unit. If they contact the opposite long edge of the defended LLO, the unit will then wheel to align to the LLO. The defending skirmish unit will then form ranks as though there were not a gap between the two units, attempting to move as many models as possible into (not technically) B2B and forming ranks behind those models as normal.

GW FAQ
Skirmishers in Combat CRB 185

Question: Low linear obstacles and Flank Charges - the rules only state the unit is counting as defending a LLO. Does a unit defending a LLO get the bonus to all arcs?
Ruling: Only the Front arc counts as being defended, even for a LLO that is magically summoned or an entrenched unit. If the charging unit charges on the flank and has not sufficient movement to charge around the LLO to get into the flank, it is allowed to straddle the LLO and charge through difficult terrain, ending up disrupted.

GW FAQ
Defended Low Linear Obstacle CRB 270

Question: How do you defend an Low linear obstacle? Aka how do you move up to it to defend it?
Ruling: You have to wheel forward, until your front rank is parallel aligned with the LLO. You do not count as defending the low linear obstacle if your front rank exceeds the LLO at any point or if your front rank is not entirely aligned to the LLO, be it due to other models or insuffcient movement .

Question: Do Characters in units count against the minimum US for scoring units?
Ruling: Yes, regardless of their unit type

Question: How is Regeneration applied for a model that suffers an unsaved wound with the Multiple Wounds (X) special rule, if the model has less than X Wounds remaining?
Ruling:
An unsaved wound with the Multiple Wounds (X) special rule causes the target to lose X Wounds (instead of 1), lost simultaneously. If the model has fewer than X Wounds remaining, it loses all its remaining Wounds, and excess wounds have no further effect (no spillover), but will count for Overkill in a Challenge. The model then attempts to Regenerate the lost Wounds.

If a troll with 3W left suffers an unsaved wound with Multiple Wounds (5), it loses its 3 remaining Wounds, then attempts to regenerate the 3 lost Wounds. The 2 potential wounds in excess have no effect.
If a skeleton suffers an unsaved wound from a cannonball with MW (D3+1), it loses it single Wound, then attempts to regenerate it. The other potential wounds in excess have no effect.

Question: Since Killing Blow / Monster Slayer only states "roll a 6 on a wound roll" and Ethereal states "cannot be wounded" - does Killing Blow / Monster Slayer with non-magical attacks actually work against Ethereal?
Ruling: No! Killing Blow / Monster Slayer states that there has to be an "unsaved wound" for it to work - but Ethereal units can only be wounded by magical attacks.

Question: Can you shoot a model with the Column of Fire Rule in a way that you hit a combat?
Ruling: No, similar to normal cannons, since you aim with a weapon that has this rule, you cannot risk shooting in a way that you hit combat (see the wording of "intended target")

Question: How is the -1 to hit from Fear applied in multi-unit combats if the Leadership test is failed?

Question: If a Skaven Character uses his verminous valour rule, does he retire, thus any special rules he contributes to the unit are lost and he cannot enter the fighting rank again in subsequent phases of combat?

However, the character has not refused a challenge, and is therefore able to move through the ranks agin in future round of combat.

Question: When can you declare a counter charge? Can you use Counter Charge if you are not able to conduct the pivot or reach the opponent?
Ruling: Counter Charge is a charge reaction which does not underly the requirements for declaring a charge. All limits of declaring Counter Charge are specificed in GW FAQ. You can declare a counter charge outside of line of sight and without having the ability to reach your opponent. If you hit an opponent unit with the counter charge move after the pivot, you count as doing accidental contact. If you cannot fully pivot, you will not move at all and if you cannot move after the pivot, you will also not move, but you still count as charging.

Question: Can you touch the flank of a unit to charge the front corner, if the full front arc/rank of the unit is already occupied by another unit of your own (or opponent)?
Ruling: If the full front arc is occupied, according to GW, you cannot charge the front at all. If even the tiniest bit of the front is unoccupied on a corner, you can do a disordered charge against the corner but note that you have to be able to position before aligning.

Question: In the notes of the Iron Hail Gun it specifies the following, "Notes: A model armed with an iron hail gun suffers no negative modifiers for firing at long range, for using the Multiple Shots (D3) special rule, or whilst making a Stand & Shoot charge reaction." Does this effect only apply to the use of the Iron Hail Gun, or the model as a whole?
Ruling: Just the iron hail gun, as the note is part of the weapon's rules, it only applies to the weapon.

Question: If you lost frenzy, can you regain it by another source?
Ruling: Yes you can. You can even re-gain frenzy by the same source, like Blood Rage. Note that if a BSB with a Banner or a character with an source that grants Frenzy (and does not state it can be regained or never lost) loses frenzy and joins a new unit, that unit won't be frenzied.

Turn Order: 4-1 Combat Phase Choose Combat & Determine Who Can Fight
Question: Can you refuse a challenge in a combat with multiple eligible characters, where at least one of those characters cannot refuse a challenge, but others could?
Ruling: No, at least one eligible character has to accept the challenge.

Question: A skirmisher unit that has formed up into Close Formation during combat must maintain this formation until it is no longer engaged at the end of the Combat phase. How does reform work while the unit is in this Close Formation (FBIGO, restrain & reform, Catching the Curs)? How does being formed up interact with Fleeing and Panic? Can you still use Chariot Runners when being Formed up?
Ruling:
Close Formation” is read as a distinct mode within Skirmish Formation: the unit is still a skirmisher, but currently “formed up” (edge‑to‑edge, ranked). While formed up, the unit behaves like a formed unit for movement purposes: pivoting and rearranging ranks/files are allowed, and it may adopt another keyword formation (e.g., Open Order) if permitted. The unit will also flee exactly like a formed unit. However, it must remain formed up until the end of the Combat phase, and does not re‑form up again when pursuing into a new enemy (it keeps the ranks/files it already has).

For Panic, the rules for Skirmishers & Panic speak of being Skirmish Formation and not of Ranks, which the formed up skirmisher formation unit still fulfills. Therefore, it will only cause panic in Skirmisher units if fleeing through and if another skirmisher unit flees through them while being formed up, they will still suffer panic.

You cannot use Chariot Runners to move with a Chariot through formed up Skirmishers.

Question: Do Ethereal Units have to make Peril tests when fleeing through another unit?
Ruling: Yes, while they cannot be wounded by magical attacks, Peril Tests cause a unit to lose a wound, not to suffer a wound, so units with the Ethereal special rule have to do peril tests just as other units do.

Question: If an enemy unit loses combat and will Give Ground off the battlefield, what are the winning unit's options?
Ruling: The winner can attempt to restrain and reform as normal. If the unit would Follow Up, they do not move as there is no enemy to move into contact with (and a unit can only overrun if the enemy is destroyed before the break test).

Question: Can Champions take 25 pts more points in Royal Clan or Wild Herd or similar Armies of Infamy?

Question: If a unit has to test for Restrain or Impetuous and wants to use the Inspiring Presence of a General,which is not inside the unit but has a modified leadership from warband, can the unit use the warband modifier on that generals modified leadership for this test?
Ruling: Yes. The unit uses the modified leadership of the general via Inspiring Presence and does not use the Warband Modifier - the General uses it. The GW FAQ notes that only "a Warband" and thus the unit itself cannot use it.

Question: When do units actually conduct Overrun?
Ruling: Overrun is a pursuit move. The unit has the choice to attempt to restrain or reform, same as for Pursuit or to Overrun and makes then a normal pursuit move bust moves directly forwards. So, the unit moves after break tests.

Question: When a Warband unit makes a leadership test and uses the Inspiring Presence of a warband general (that is not in the unit). How are the multiple warband bonuses applied to this leadership test? Note that this question only adresses the warband modifier and refers to the wording of the Warband special rule.
Ruling: Only the warband modifier of the Generals unit (if he is in a warband unit) is used. If the general is not in a warband unit, then no warband modifier can be claimed.

Question: A unit affected by certain spells (Earthen Ramparts, Miasmic Mirage), formation (marching column) or that has rallied cannot charge or make a charge moves. How does this interact with Random Movers contacting enemies, Counter Charge or Pursuit Into a Fresh Enemy?
Ruling: Since all these count as charging, and therefore as charge  moves for special rules like Frenzy or Furious Charge and Impact Hits, you cannot conduct these  when  under such effects.

Question: When charging a unit in an arc that features an incomplete rank, how are you to make contact with that unit? What happens if you overrun or pursuit into such a unit, but only hit the template or rather footprint?
Ruling:
If charging, Use the footprint of the unit, extending the incomplete rank or file to be complete, and have the charging unit make contact (and maximize contact with) models who would be in those positions.
If Overruning or during a pursuit, you only make contact with such an unit if you hit actual models. In that case, you would conduct your move wheeling to maximise towards the footprint of the unit.

Question: Do fanatics now die when moving through a unit that is entrenched or under the effect of Earthen Ramparts?
Ruling: If the unit is under the effect of Earthen Ramparts but wasn’t charged, they hit the unit since earthen ramparts specifies it only works if charged. Against entrenched or earthen ramparts when charged, the fanatics hit the obstacle and die.

Question: When a character or champion retires from combat, is moved for a challenge, or moves through the ranks, does this count as the unit moving for the purpose of related special rules (such as being 'entrenched')?
Ruling: No. The character (or champion) counts as moving when they retire, but the unit itself does not.

Question: Can I choose for reserves to enter during any player’s turn?
Ruling: No, only on your own turns.

Question: Do modifiers to the To Hit roll apply when using the Seal of Parravon?
Ruling: Yes. The Seal of Parravon refers to a roll of 3 on the To Hit table before modifiers (i.e., the result after consulting the table, not the natural dice roll). Modifiers are applied as normal.

Question: Can the champion of a unit which swapped their shields for another weapon still buy a magical shield? And can the champion chose to wield a separate equipment than the unit (if he wears a mundane/magical weapon?)?
Ruling: Yes, just like how a character doesn't have to buy a generic shield in order to have a magic one. You just need the shield as a possible option to access the magic version. Yes, the champion can use a different weapon option if he has access to.

Question: If Chalice of Dark Rain is active, can a casket of souls use a magical missile? Are wailing dirges affected by it?
Ruling: Only the range of missile weapons is halved´, so the range of Magic Missiles, Wailing Dirge, Breath Weapons and similar rules are not affected (Sky Lantern Bombs), but war machines cannot shoot at all. Since the casket's magic missile is a shooting attack, it cannot be used in such a turn.

Question: Can Sappers use their ability "Dig in!" in every command phase or only in their own?
Ruling: The wording of the special rule "Dig in!" has priority over the general rules for command abilities, thus the special rule can be used in every command phase.

Question: If a unit of skirmishers takes casualties and has no other choice than to remove models in a way that two or more characters that have joined said unit lose coherency with the unit, what happens to the characters?
Ruling: Any model out of coherency, including characters, is removed from play as casualty.

Question: When do you actually conduct accidental contact during a charge? Do you get a charge reaction against it? What happens if you have Fly? And what happens if the original charge target fled?
Ruling:
If wheeling around the obstacle would cause you to do a failed charge, or if the unit is not able to wheel around the obstacle unit at all, you conduct accidental contact during a charge. The charging unit only counts as having redirected prior so it can make contact - you don't get a charge reaction, which only is available after a unit is selected as charge target during a redirect or charge declaration.

A charging unit must endeavour to bring as many models as possible within its front rank into base contact with models in the charged unit. That is the highest priority and the unit must use Fly (X) if needed. You determine if Fly (X) is needed when the unit starts its charge move. If the charging unit with Fly(X)  would make a failed charge and ends on top of the enemy unit, do accidental contact. However, if you fly over/behind the enemy unit, you cannot do accidental contact as it is not the enemy unit, but the missing charge distance that leads to the failed charge.
If the charge target declared flee or is fleeing for any reason, you do not conduct accidental contact during a charge at all, as you have to check for accidental contact during Running Down the Foe. During Running down the Foe, you charge as normally and you never make a failed charge, thus you always try to wheel or move around the obstacle unit. Only if you cannot do that, you will make accidental contact. This means, in most caes, that units with Fly (X) or Skirmishers go over or around obstacle units.
Referenced Rules:

Question: Q: Redress the Ranks requires models to be added (or subtracted) from the left and right side of the unit "as equally as possible." What happens when it is only possible to add models to one side of the unit?
Ruling:
Redress the Ranks can at most add one more model to the left side than the right (or vice versa). If one side is blocked, then a unit can only redress to add a single model to the opposite side.

When removing models, the last models to remove must be the characters, then the command group, always keeping the standard bearer in the front rank and as close to the centre as possible. Command group models removed from the front rank must go to the second rank (and third in case of a single column). Characters removed from the front rank must go to the rear rank. The player choses the position of all models in their respective back ranks. When adding models to the front rank, the opposite order must be followed: first the command group, then the characters, before rank and file models. The position of added models can be chosen by the controlling player, but must respect the positioning rule for the command group and for characters: standard bearer as close to the centre as possible, command group models to either side, characters anywhere in the front rank. Note that characters may be placed among the command group.

Question: Is a unit with Random Movement affected by modifiers applying to their Movement characteristic, such as terrain or spells?

Question: The spell Hidden Pathways allows the target to "perform a Quick Turn, even if it would not normally be able to do so." What exactly does this mean?
