Question: If a Character is placed in the rear rank outside of combat because there is no room for them in the front rank, do they count as retired? What happens if there is also no space in the rear rank or he shrinks back into the fighting/front rank? What happens if there is space again for characters that retired because of too many characters or there are only places in the fighting rank left due to shrinking units?
Ruling:
A Character that is not leading from the front is considered retired and cannot confer Inspiring Presence, Hold Your Ground, Aura abilities or similar static benefits unless a rule explicitly states otherwise. Any benefits from spells with the range 'Self' are lost, but spells and abilities that targeted other units or are resolved for global effects remain in effect. Retired models will be counted towards the Units Unit Strength and towards the formation to determine rank bonus, combat order and marching column. They are still considered part of the unit for any check on unit type, model special rule affiliation (unit 'consists entirely' etc.) and target legality (ethereal, unbreakable etc.)

If the character cannot be placed in the rear rank, place him in the closest spot from the rear that is away from a fighting or front rank to retire him. Adjacent characters can be placed behind the rear rank if they retire.

If the unit shrinks down and the character returns by this to the front or fighting rank only because no other position away from a fighting rank is available, he unretires after all casualties are removed, after the initiative step and after any panic checks are resolved, but if this happens in combat he counts as having stepped forward. Outside of combat the usual rules for unretiring characters take place and characters return to the front rank if the formation allows to.

Question: When a character leaves a unit, how is that character affected by any spells or effects that modify the unit's movement? Do they maintain the unit formation they were in, or always move as a skirmisher?

Any spells or effects (positive or negative) affect the character's movement during the Remaining Moves phase in which the character leaves the unit. This means that if the unit is affected by Miasmic Mirage, the character cannot march, and if the unit is affected by Steed of Shadows, the character may move using Fly (12). If for any reason the character does not follow the Lone Character rules when not in a unit (such as a character on a light chariot), then they must adhere to the normal movement rules for their respective unit type when leaving the unit.

Question: Q: The 1.5 errata states that "Any model that is within a fighting rank Movement of the enemy unit can fight." The Random Movement special rule states that "Models with this special rule do not have a normal Movement characteristic. Instead, a dice roll is given (2D6, for example). A) Because the unit does not have a normal movement characteristic when not actively moving, treat the movement value during combat as M (-). This means that models with Random Movement can only make attacks when in base contact with an enemy model. Hello world!?
B) Those units still have a Movement characteristic that deviates from the norm. Question: Are Fanatics units?
Ruling:
Yes, a fanatic is a unit (except for all cases that are explained and listed under their unit entry) as it has a model profile, including characteristics, special rules, equipment etc. This means they work as any other unit, with the following exceptions:
- cannot be charged or have attacks directed against them (with the exception of enemy shooting attacks, against which they count as lone characters) and cannot be targeted by any spells (with the exception of enemy magic missiles), not even by their owner.
- does not engage with other units, but follows the rules for fanatic movement when hitting them.
- do not give away victory points when dying.
- their special rule which allows units to move through them forces units to charge through fanatics towards their charge target.
Note that fanatics being units will force the following interactions:
- They count as unit for the 1" check of give ground, which is not being disabled by the Fanatic Movement rule.
- Fanatics can hit each other (see the COMFAQ entry for units destroyed while moving) and can never leave the board.
- They provide cover and will cause ambushers and units returning from offside the battlefield to keep distance to them.
- They will cause peril tests when units flee through them in addition to the Fanatic Ball & Chain rule.
- They will cause panic in units and will potentially cause units to flee from them if the fanatic is the closest enemy unit.
- Score domination.

Question: How is cover determined?
Ruling: Cover is a measure of how obscured LoS is. How much of the "other model or unit" is visible or obscured is determined considering the definition of LoS, including rules that define when models do or don't block Line of Sight (Large Target, Insignificant, Vantage Point). This means, among others, that non-Large models do not provide cover if the shooting or target unit is a Large Target, that models not on a Vantage Point (Hill) do not provide cover if the shooting or target unit is entirely on a Vantage Point (Hill), and that Insignificant models never provide cover. Remember that Large Targets never benefit from cover. Note that for terrain categories that do not have a specific rule for Line of Sight (e.g. buildings, linear obstacles, ruins, battlefield decoration…), Line of Sight has to be determined by checking the actual "true" Line of Sight from the model, if not stated otherwise by the tournament organizer.

Question: Do special rules conferred by a model's weapon apply to attacks made by that model's mount?
Ruling:
No. Any rules conferred by a weapon, be it magical or mundane, apply only to attacks made with that weapon. This can include, but is not limited to, rules unique to a specific type of weapon, special rules that apply to a particular weapon, or special rules that apply to a magic weapon. For example, if a Wizard is armed with the Sword of Swiftness, attacks made with that weapon have the Strikes First special rule, but the Wizard cannot claim that wielding the weapon allows them to cast Assailment spells at Initiative 10.

To give another example, if a model has a special rule unique to its faction that grants additional rules to a hand weapon (the crew of an Orc Boar Chariot have the Choppas special rule, for example), that rule applies only to actual hand weapons carried by riders or chariot crew, not to weapons belonging to mounts or draft animals that 'count as' hand weapons.

Question: Can the Hagtree Fetish be used to re-roll rolls To Wound caused by a Bound Spell?
Ruling: No. Bound Spells are cast by the item they are bound to, whilst Arcane Items such as the Hagtree Fetish affect spells cast by their bearer. Therefore, unless an item specifies it has an effect upon Bound Spells, it does not.

Question: If a Wizard engaged in a challenge knows and uses an Assailment spell that can hit multiple enemy models (such as Assailment spells that use a template), are multiple enemy models hit, or is it only the other participant in the challenge that can be hit?
Ruling: When an Assailment spell is cast in a challenge, it can only hit the other participant in the challenge.

Question: Does the Waystalker’s Hawk-eyed Archer rule apply to magic items that allow the bearer to cast a Magic Missile?
Ruling: No, it applies only to the Waystalker’s Asrai longbow, or to ranged magic weapons.

Question: What happens if I wish to accept a challenge to fight a Warrior's Duel but do not have any single Wound champions in my army?
Ruling: Roll off to determine who takes the first turn as normal.

Question: Can Korhil Lionmane or a Chracian Chieftain join a unit of White Lions of Chrace?
Ruling: Yes.

Question: Can a Bretonnian army pray for the Blessing of the Lady if it includes an allied contingent?
Ruling: Yes, however an allied contingent of Bretonnians taken as part of any other army cannot pray. In order for Bretonnians to pray, the army they are part of must have the Blessings of the Lady rule, which only Kingdom of Bretonnia armies have.

Question: Can the Infernal Puppet be used against a Bound spell?
Ruling: Yes.

Question: What constitutes a 'move'?
Ruling: Quite simply, if you touch a model or unit and change its position in any way, it has moved. There are some exceptions to this, a war machine that pivots does not count as having moved, for example, but in the vast majority of cases, the term 'move' follows the broadest definition; if a model or unit shifts its position or changes its location, it has moved.

Question: The rulebook lists the minimum size of battlefield as 30" x 44" for games of up to 1,000 points, 44" x 60" for 1,001 to 3,000 points and 44" x 90" for games of 3,001 points or above. Do we have to use these sizes?
Ruling: No. These are the minimum recommended sizes. The normal size battlefield for a game of between 2,000 and 3,000 points is 48" x 72" (4' x 6') and players are encouraged to use this. The minimum sizes are based on the folding card battlefields Games Workshop produces. These are ideal when space is an issue or for smaller games. For example, we prefer a 44" x 60" battlefield for a game of 1,000 or 1,500 points, rather than the more traditional 48" x 48" battlefield. We find the smaller, rectangular shape more pleasing.

Question: If I give armour runes to an Anvil of Doom, does the Anvil itself benefit, or just the crew?
Ruling: Just the crew.

Question:
How many spells can a Wizard attempt to cast during
a single phase? For example, if a Wizard knows a Magical Vortex and a Magic Missile, can they attempt to cast both during the same Shooting phase?
Ruling: A Wizard can only cast a number of spells up to their Level of Wizardry per turn, but can attempt to cast multiple spells during a single phase. In other words, should a Level 2 Wizard know two Magic Missiles and one Magical Vortex (three spells), they can only cast two of them per turn, but may cast both during the same phase.

Question: Can my Battle Standard Bearer have a higher Leadership than my General?
Ruling: No. As stated on page 203, the General is the character with the highest Leadership. If this means not upgrading the character with the highest Leadership in your army to be your Battle Standard Bearer so that they can be your General, so be it.

Question: When a 'Dug In' unit of Skirmishers is charged by an enemy unit, does it lose that status?
Ruling: No.

Question: Players have choices to make throughout the game. If both players have the same choice to make at the same time, who chooses first?
Ruling: The active player always chooses first. Sometimes this will  be advantageous, sometimes not, but choosing first is the active player’s prerogative.

Question: If a unit of Night Goblins that is engaged in combat still contains any unreleased Fanatics, can they be released whilst the unit is engaged?
Ruling: Provided they can be placed within 3" of their concealing unit and not touching the bases of any other models, yes.

Question: If Harald Gemunsen issues a second challenge using his Skilled Duellist special rule, he can fight again immediately. Can his opponent in that challenge fight again?
Ruling: Yes. If Harald's second challenge is accepted it is fought immediately, meaning both Harald and his opponent can fight. However, Harald's mount may not fight, and nor may his opponent's.

Question: Some attacks allow a specific model within a unit to be targeted. Can such an attack be used to break the coherency of a unit of Skirmishers and cause other models to be removed as well?
Ruling: No. As stated on page 184, you cannot remove a model from a unit of Skirmishers if doing so would cause the unit to lose coherency. However, if an attack targets a specific model (such as a champion or a character), that model must be removed if the attack reduces it to zero Wounds. In such cases, simply replace the removed model with another model belonging to the same unit, one that could be removed as a casualty, in order to maintain unit coherency.

Question: If the spell Arcane Urgency is used to move a unit with Random Movement, can the unit move into contact with an enemy unit?
Ruling: No. Whilst a unit with Random Movement can move into base contact with an enemy unit during the Compulsory Moves sub-phase, Arcane Urgency causes units to move when the spell is cast, during the Remaining Moves sub-phase.

Question: Are units required to make Panic tests due to the actions of friendly models? For example, if a Wizard miscasts and rolls a 2-4 on the Miscast table, causing a Dimensional Cascade and inflicting sufficient casualties on a friendly unit to cause it to Panic, must that unit make a Panic test?
Ruling: Yes (that example sounds to us like something that really would cause panic amongst the ranks!).

Question: If my opponent and I have agreed to play a 2,000 points game but my army is not exactly 2,000 points (it's 1,997 points, for example), can I take two of something limited to 0-1 per 1,000 points by the army composition list I'm using?
Ruling: Yes. Such limitations are based on the size of the game you are playing rather than the exact points value of your army.

Category: Arcane Journal: The War of Settra's Fury
Question: Must a unit be in a Phalanx in order to not become Disrupted when charged by a unit with First Charge?
Ruling: Yes. Units do not gain the benefit of being in a particular formation if they are not in that formation.
Referenced Rules: Arcane Journal: The War of Settra's Fury

Question: How does Master Rune of Adamant work on an Anvil of Doom?
Ruling: It increases the Toughness of the crew, but not of the anvil itself.

Question: When are Ambushers placed into reserve and when is this declared?
Ruling: If your army includes any Ambushers that you wish to hold in reserve, set those units aside before deployment begins, making it clear to your opponent that they are Ambushers and will be held in reserve, rather than be deployed with the rest of your army.

Question: Can a Royal Herald take hits on behalf of a Monarch that is engaged in a challenge?
Ruling: No.

Category: Arcane Journal: Armies of Grand Cathay
Question: Heavenly Beacon allows you to modify the roll by +1 or -1 when rolling to determine if Ambushers arrive. Is this cumulative? In other words, is it +2 or -2 if I have two Sky Lanterns?
Ruling: No, it's not cumulative. You may apply a +1 or -1 modifier if you have one or more Sky Lanterns.
Referenced Rules: Arcane Journal: Armies of Grand Cathay

Category: Warhammer: The Old World Matched Play Guide
Question: Can a unit control more than one object on the battlefield? For example, can a unit control a special feature, a battlefield objective, and a secondary objective such as a baggage train, all at the same time?
Ruling: No. If a unit is in a position to control two or more such objects, you must choose one for it to control.
Referenced Rules: Warhammer: The Old World Matched Play Guide

Question: If my army includes a Mercenary character, can I make them my General?
Ruling: No. An army’s General must be one of the characters listed in the 'characters' section of the army composition list you are using.

Question: Can a Steam Tank's steam cannon fire grapeshot?
Ruling: Yes. Grapeshot can be fired by any cannon (i.e., any weapon that fires using the 'Cannon Fire' special rule), as described on page 226 of the *Warhammer: The Old World* rulebook.

Question: For the purposes of other upgrades, what types of armour are the Armour of Silvered Steel and the Armour of Meteoric Iron?
Ruling: If a suit of magic armour gives an armour value of 6+, it should be considered light armour. If it gives an armour value of 5+, it should be considered heavy armour, and if it gives an armour value of 4+ or better, it should be considered full plate armour.

Question: When shooting a cannon, a line of sight is required to the target point, but what about the strike point?
Ruling: A cannon does not require a line of sight to the strike point. However, if anything that would stop a cannonball from bouncing (see 5. Crunch, on page 227) lies between the target point and the strike point, the cannonball will hit it and stop. In other words, you cannot use a high result on the Artillery dice to 'glitch' a cannonball through an impregnable obstacle.

Question: If a Fanatic moves into contact with a unit that's engaged in combat, does it hit the unit(s) that unit is engaged with as well?
Ruling: When a Fanatic moves into contact with another unit, it continues in a straight line until it can be placed back on the battlefield. Any units that line passes through are hit. Units the line does not pass through are not hit.

Question: When are line of sight and cover determined for a unit that declares a Stand & Shoot charge reaction?
Ruling: When the charge reaction is declared.

Question: If a specific natural roll triggers an effect, is that effect still triggered if the dice is re-rolled and the re-roll gives a different result?
Ruling: No. When you re-roll a dice, the previous roll is discarded. This includes any effects that roll may have triggered.

Question: If I take a Black Orc Warboss as the General of a Nomadic Waaagh!, can I take a unit of Boar Boys as a Core choice?
Ruling: No. A unit of Boar Boys can only be taken as a Core choice if your General is an Orc Warboss.

Question: How does the Dark Coven army special rule from the Wild Herd Army of Infamy interact with the Plague Chalice?
Ruling: In cases such as this, both outcomes can apply. If a natural double is rolled, the spell is cast as a perfect invocation and the caster suffers a hit from the Plague Chalice. However, the caster and any other members of their coven will then also suffer the effects of a roll on the Miscast table, as per the Dark Coven special rule.

Question: Does a unit with the Blood Greed special rule always roll only a single D6 when making a Pursuit roll, or only whilst Frenzied?
Ruling: Only whilst Frenzied.

Category: Arcane Journal: Tomb Kings of Khemri
Question: The crew of Tomb Guard chariots are equipped with shields. Does this improve the Armour Value of the model from 4+ to 3+?
Ruling: No. A chariot's given Armour Value takes into account such equipment.
Referenced Rules: Arcane Journal: Tomb Kings of Khemri

Question: If a unit upon which Earthen Ramparts has been cast  is obliged to declare a charge (if the unit is Frenzied or Impetuous, for example), must it do so? If so, can it make a charge move?
Ruling: Earthen Ramparts does not prevent a unit from declaring a charge, it prevents it from charging. In other words, yes the unit must declare a charge if obliged to do so. However, because the unit cannot charge, it does not move at all and the charge is failed.

Question: Some monsters have weapons with notes that state they must make, or may choose to make, one attack, or one additional attack, with that weapon in combat. Can they make more than one attack with such weapons?
Ruling: No. If it is noted on a weapon's profile that the model may or must make a specific number of attacks with that weapon, normal attacks or otherwise, that's how many attacks it makes with that weapon.

Question: Can a Wood Elf Realms army that includes an allied contingent place an additional wood using the Woodland Ambush rule?
Ruling: Yes. Note however that an allied contingent of Wood Elves taken as part of another army cannot.

Question: How do I determine the centre of a unit of Skirmishers?
Ruling: The centre is the point that is equally distant from the models at the extremities of the group. However, when considering blast templates, the purpose of placing a blast template over the centre of a unit is to ensure a significant number of models are underneath it. In the case of a unit of Skirmishers, this is not always possible. Therefore, you may place the central hole of a blast template over the model closest to the centre of a unit of Skirmishers.

Question: Does the Martial Prowess special rule allow models to make supporting attacks with weapons that do not have the Fight in Extra Rank special rule?
Ruling: No. Martial Prowess grants the ability to make supporting attacks to the flank or rear, as well as to its front. It does not grant the ability to make supporting attacks to models not normally able to do so.

Question: Units must make a Panic test when a nearby friendly unit with a Unit Strength of 5 or more is destroyed. When is Unit Strength counted – from the start of the turn, the start of the phase, or the point at which the unit is destroyed?
Ruling: From the start of the phase during which the unit was destroyed. For example, if a friendly unit with a Unit Strength of 10 is destroyed by enemy shooting during a single Shooting phase, it causes panic in nearby friendly units. Players are not expected to remember the Unit Strength of every unit from turn to turn or phase to phase, but should keep track of Unit Strength during each phase.

Question: If a unit that has 'Dug In' becomes engaged in combat, does it lose that status if a model within it accepts or declines a challenge and moves through the ranks?
Ruling: No.

Question: What is the furthest a model can move?
Ruling:
No model can move more than twice its Movement characteristic or, when movement is determined by a dice roll (such as when a unit charges or flees), further than the distance rolled. There are, of course, exceptions to this, the most obvious being when a unit in Marching Column marches at triple its Movement characteristic, when models are moved by the effect of a spell, when a unit is obliged to continue its move rather than end up 'on top' of another unit, and obligatory moves (such as when a charging unit wheels to align with the enemy, or when a unit pivots before fleeing).

Note that when a unit wheels, those at its rear do not really follow a long, curving path, as it might appear when moving a large block of models on the table. In reality, those models would take a more direct route, following the path of the front rank and resuming their formation behind it. Accordingly, we do not measure the distance moved by models in the rear ranks of a wheeling unit.

Note also that, when a unit is permitted a free manoeuvre before or after moving, this is free in that it does not count towards the move itself, but the limitation that no model can move more than twice its Movement characteristic applies within the manoeuvre.

Question: A unit of Empire Road Wardens may replace its crossbows with braces of pistols for +1 point per model. If it does so, must the Captain (champion) pay an additional +2 points to do the same?
Ruling: No. If the entire unit replaces its crossbows with braces of pistols, that includes the Captain. If the unit is armed with crossbows, the Captain has the option to replace theirs with a brace of pistols or a repeater pistol.

Question: When deploying armies, must units be placed completely within their deployment zone?
Ruling: Yes.

Question: Can a character with the Shield of the Lady special rule retire to the rear of their unit after issuing a challenge, enabling them to avoid their opponent's attacks?
Ruling: No. Once a challenge has been issued and accepted neither combatant can retire until the challenge is resolved. Chivalry demands it.

Question: When fighting a Warrior's Duel challenge between two unit champions, are such things as magic standards carried by their units counted?
Ruling: No. A Warrior's Duel is fought between the two participants alone, without any support from their units.

Question: Casting the same Enchantment or Hex spells on a unit more than once has no further effect, but what about spells with a range of 'Self' that affect all units within a certain distance of the caster?
Ruling: Unless stated otherwise, such spells are not cumulative and casting them multiple times will have no further effect.

Question: If one participant in a challenge causes Impact Hits or makes Stomp Attacks, where are they directed?
Ruling: Impact Hits are resolved prior to issuing challenges. Stomp Attacks may be directed against the other participant in the challenge.

Question: If a unit's fighting rank is engaged with two enemy units, one of which is a lone character engaged in a challenge, can models within the unit's fighting rank ignore the character even if they are closer to it than to the other enemy unit, or are their attacks lost?
Ruling: Models not engaged in a challenge cannot direct their attacks against models that are. In other words, any models that would normally have to direct their attacks against the character are free to direct them instead against the other unit their unit is engaged with.

Question: If a character with the Mark of Nurgle (for example) is mounted on a chariot with the Mark of Chaos Undivided, does the chariot benefit from the character's Mark, or do I have to pay the points to give the chariot the Mark of Nurgle for it to gain the same benefits?
Ruling: If you want a chariot mount to have the same benefits from a Mark of Chaos that its rider has, you have to pay the points to give the chariot the Mark of Chaos.

Question: Can a unit that rallies and reforms during the Rally Fleeing Units sub-phase move during the Movement phase?
Ruling: Yes.

Question: Does a weapon's AP reduce the armour value of the Armour of Meteoric Iron?
Ruling: No.

Question: When does a detachment determine which arc of an enemy unit it will charge into when making a supporting charge?
Ruling: When it is moved, at the end of the Charge Moves sub-phase.

Category: Warhammer: The Old World Matched Play Guide
Question: When using Domination as a secondary objective, do you get the Victory Points for having more than double the enemy's Unit Strength in a table quarter if there are no enemy models in that quarter?
Ruling: No. To be more than double the enemy’s Unit Strength, the enemy has to have some models in the quarter. If they have none and you do, you gain the VP bonus for that achievement instead.
Referenced Rules: Warhammer: The Old World Matched Play Guide

Question: Are the effects of ‘Eternal Taskmaster’ cumulative?
Ruling: No.

Category: Arcane Journal: Armies of Grand Cathay
Question: Are the effects of the Grand Cannon's Thunderous Impact special rule cumulative? In other words, if a unit is within range of two strike points, does it suffer a -2 modifier to its Movement characteristic?
Ruling: No, it's not cumulative.
Referenced Rules: Arcane Journal: Armies of Grand Cathay

Question: Does the Daemon Heart increase its user’s Dispel Range?
Ruling: No.

Question: When a model fights, must it make all of its attacks, or can it choose to make fewer?
Ruling: If a model is able to fight, it must make all of its attacks.

Question: Can a Steam Tank's Engineer Commander and steam cannon both shoot during the same turn?
Ruling: Yes. The Engineer Commander doesn't fire the steam cannon, imagine there's a (very hot and bothered) crew hidden away inside the Steam Tank whose endeavours leave the Engineer Commander free to fire their own weapon.

Question: Does a unit that includes a Grail Monk with a Blessed Triptych lose Stubborn if the Grail Monk is killed before the rule can be used?
Ruling: No. As per the errata, a unit that includes a Blessed Triptych becomes Stubborn, regardless of whether or not the model that purchased that upgrade has been killed or not.

Question: Can you choose not to roll for the arrival of Ambushers during your Start of Turn sub-phase?
Ruling: No. Unless the unit itself or the scenario being played has a special rule that changes the way in which Ambushers arrive, you must roll for their arrival during each of your turns, from round two onwards. However, any special rules that affect the arrival of Ambushers which take effect after the Start of Turn sub-phase but before the Compulsory Moves sub-phase may be used as normal, regardless of the result of the Ambushers roll.

Question: Can a model that chooses to Stand & Shoot (or Fire & Flee) as a charge reaction attempt to cast a Magic Missile or Magical Vortex?
Ruling: No. As stated on page 143, models that know such spells can attempt to cast them when chosen during the active player's Shooting phase. Perhaps obviously, this includes Bound spells.

Question: The Bow of Loren allows a Wood Elf character to make a number of shots equal to their Attacks characteristic. How does this interact with Enchanted Arrows?
Ruling: When firing an Enchanted Arrow it is assumed the model is firing only once, as is the norm. Therefore, one of the shots fired from the Bow of Loren can be made using an Enchanted Arrow, the other shots are resolved using ordinary (i.e., not Enchanted) arrows.

Question: Do magic missiles that require the caster to draw a line from their base require a target?
Ruling: No. As stated in the spell's description, simply draw a line from the caster's base. Any model the line hits is hit by the spell.

Question: Is an 'Entrenched' unit protected on all four sides, or just its front?
Ruling: Just its front, as stated on page 270 of the Warhammer: the Old World rulebook.

Question: Can a model armed with two hand weapons choose to fight with just one hand weapon?
Ruling: Yes. As noted on page 213, unless stated otherwise, all models are assumed to be equipped with a hand weapon. A model with two has, by definition, two and may choose to fight with just one, foregoing the Extra Attacks (+1) special rule in favour of some other benefit.

Question: In a Nomadic Waaagh!, I can take one Black Orc Boss per Black Orc Chariot. If I take a Black Orc Boss mounted on a chariot, does that count?
Ruling: No. You can take one Black Orc Boss per Black Orc Chariot taken as a Core or Rare choice. It does not matter what the Boss is mounted on.

Question: If a unit that is subject to any Leadership modifiers uses the General's Inspiring Presence rule (or any other rule that allows a unit to use the Leadership of a nearby character), does the unit ignore those modifiers?
Ruling: No, the modifier will still apply. For example, if a unit loses a round of combat to a Terror causing enemy, the -1 modifier to Leadership caused by Terror applies to whichever Leadership characteristic the unit makes its Break test against, be that its own or that of a nearby character.

Question: Can a cannon that is on a hill target a point on the ground if woods, a building or a hill lies between it and that point?
Ruling: No, a cannon cannot shoot over such obstacles, even if it is on a hill. However, a stone thrower can if it chooses to fire indirectly.

Question: Sometimes, when a unit of Skirmishers charges or is charged, some of the models cannot move far enough to form up with the rest of the unit. What happens to those models?
Ruling: The unit loses coherency, as described on page 184. This means models belonging to the unit must be removed from play as casualties until the unit becomes coherent.

Question: If I mark the position of a unit then proceed to move it before putting it back where it was and moving it again, does this count as a take-back?
Ruling: Yes, absolutely.

Question: Can the champion in a unit of Royal Clan Warriors or Hammerers put weapon runes on a gromril great axe or great hammer?
Ruling: No. Weapon runes can only be inscribed upon a hand weapon or great weapon, as defined in the Warhammer: the Old World rulebook. The Royal Clan Warriors' gromril great axes and the Hammerers' great hammers are unique types of weapon, each with their own profile and rules.

Question: If one participant in a challenge is killed, can other models engaged in the same combat direct their Attacks against the survivor during the same Combat phase when it is their turn to fight?
Ruling: No. Even if one participant in a challenge has been slain, the challenge is considered to be ongoing until the end of the current Combat phase.

Question: How are Victory Points scored for a Night Goblin unit that includes one or more Fanatics once its Fanatic(s) have been released?
Ruling: Fanatics are an upgrade for the unit; their cost is included when working out VP for the unit itself. In other words, the death of an individual Fanatic is not worth any VP, but destroying the unit it was concealed within will earn you the VP for the Fanatic as part of the unit's points cost.

Question: If a character joins a unit of Skin Wolves, can they be transfigured by the Warped Form special rule?
Ruling: No.

Question: Can a unit upon which Earthen Ramparts has been cast make a Counter Charge charge reaction?
Ruling: No.

Question: Can a Necrosphinx make more than one attack each turn with its Decapitating strike?
Ruling: No. The decapitating strike profile must be used as noted – to make one additional attack.

Category: Arcane Journal: Armies of Grand Cathay
Question: Mastery of the Elemental Winds can only be used once per turn, but is this once per Wizard or once per army?
Ruling: Once per army.
Referenced Rules: Arcane Journal: Armies of Grand Cathay

Question: Models in a fighting rank cannot fight if they are killed before they have a chance to fight. But can models in a second fighting rank (in the case of units within the Press of Battle rule) fight if the model in front is slain, and can a model make a supporting attack if the model(s) in the fighting ranks(s) in front of it are slain?
Ruling: Yes. Unless they have been killed, models that are in a fighting rank or that are able to make supporting attacks can do so as normal. In other words, casualties inflicted reduce, firstly, the number of models in the fighting rank(s) that are able to fight (starting with the first fighting rank) and, secondly, the number of models in the 'supporting rank' that are able to fight.

Question: Can a unit with Defensive Stakes be hit by Impact Hits or Stomp Attacks by a charging enemy?
Ruling: Yes. Whilst the stakes might do tremendous damage to 'cavalry' and 'chariots', the momentum of such models when they charge will carry them into the archers, although they may be turned to kindling in the attempt.

Question: When a model hits an enemy unit using the Deathblow special rule, does that hit benefit from that model's special rules?
Ruling: Yes.

Question: Bearing two or more Obsidian Lodestones gives better Magic Resistance, but does an Obsidian Lodestone improve Magic Resistance granted by a different source?
Ruling: No.

Question: Does an allied contingent have to abide by the restrictions given in the army composition list it is drawn from?
Ruling: Yes. An allied contingent is a small army within a large army, made using a Grand Army or Army of Infamy composition list. Within a 2,000 points army, for example, an allied contingent of 500 points would have to spend at least 125 points on Core units, could spend no more than 250 points on characters, and would be unable to include any units limited to 0-1 per 1,000 points.

Question: Can a cannon target a point on the ground if another unit lies between it and that point?
Ruling: Not unless that cannon is on a hill and the unit is not. However, as above, a stone thrower can if it chooses to fire indirectly.

Question: Before a Steam Tank charges, can it use the Steam Power special rule to increase its Movement?
Ruling: No. The Steam Power special rule can be used by a Steam Tanks, a model that cannot march, instead of marching. In other words, in instances where most models or units would increase their movement by marching, a Steam Tank can instead make use of the Steam Power special rule. Charging is not such an instance.

Question: If my Battle Standard Bearer refuses a challenge and retires from combat, can other units still benefit from their "Hold Your Ground" special rule?
Ruling: Not whilst that character's unit is still engaged with the model that issued the challenge. Battle standards are somewhat less inspirational whilst being used as a blanket to hide beneath.

Question: Does the Armour Bane (X) special rule apply to spells cast by a model with the rule, such as Assailment spells, Magic Missiles or Magical Vortexes?
Ruling: No.

Question: If a Wizard has a special rule that applies when they attack an enemy, such as Killing Blow or Armour Bane, is that special rule applied to any spells they may cast?
Ruling: Absolutely not.

Question: How does a unit of Skirmishers form up when charged by two or more different enemy units from different directions?
Ruling: The Skirmishers should form up against the first charging unit to move into contact with them. The remaining enemy units then charge the formed Skirmishers. If any units are unable to complete their charge moves, their charges are failed.

Question: Can a Black Orc Boss take a Black Orc Chariot as a mount in an army made using the Orc and Goblin Tribes Grand Army composition list?
Ruling: They cannot. With heavy hearts, we must inform everyone who asked that that option is only available in armies made using the Nomadic Waaagh! Army of Infamy composition list.

Question: Can a missile weapon be used in combat?
Ruling: No.

Question: Can a model use a Breath weapon after marching?
Ruling: No. A model cannot shoot during the Shooting phase if it marched during the preceding Movement phase and, although they work differently to most missile weapons, Breath weapons are a type of missile weapon.

Question: If a unit charges an enemy unit upon which Earthen Ramparts has been cast, must it follow all the rules for charging an enemy unit behind a defended low linear obstacle, even though there is no such physical terrain between the two units?
Ruling: Yes. A unit upon which Earthen Ramparts has been cast counts as being behind a defended low linear obstacle when charged. Think of the spell’s effect as representing a magically manifested obstacle between, rather than a physical terrain feature.

Question: What happens if a Hit is rolled on the Scatter dice for an object that moves in a random direction, do I use the small arrow on the Hit icon to determine the direction?
Ruling: Essentially, objects that move in a random direction scatter, as described on page 95. Such objects only move in the direction shown by the small arrow on the Hit icon if the rules tell you they do so. Otherwise, the object does not move.

Question: Is Overkill counted by or against a champion in a challenge, or does it only count for characters?
Ruling: Overkill counts in all challenges, whether the participants are characters or champions.

Question: Can a unit move whilst locked in combat?
Ruling: No.

Question: What happens to a Fanatic that moves into or through the front arc of a unit of Bretonnian Peasant Bowmen equipped with 'defensive stakes'?
Ruling: Nothing good. Defensive stakes function very much like linear terrain, therefore a Fanatic that moves into contact with a row of defensive stakes, from any direction, comes to a very sudden stop and is removed from play as a casualty.

Question: Do runes inscribed upon a Doomseeker’s whirling blades of death apply to Impact Hits?
Ruling: Yes. As stated under Whirlwind of Death, Impact Hits caused by a Doomseeker are resolved using the profile of its whirling blades of death, which includes any runes the weapon is inscribed with.

Question: Whilst Drain Magic is in play, does it increase the Casting Value of Bound spells?
Ruling: Yes.

Question: If the musician and/or standard bearer in a unit of Slayers are models that have been upgraded to Giant Slayers, what happens if they are slain, is their instrument and/or standard picked up by another Giant Slayer or by a Troll Slayer?
Ruling:
It rather depends on the models that remain in the unit. If any Giant Slayers remain, they will pick up the instrument or standard, replacing the slain models like for like. If no Giant Slayers remain, a Troll Slayer will take their place.

Note also that Giant Slayers are not unit champions. Thus in a unit of Slayers, the standard bearer would be the last model removed.

Question: Does a unit of Battle Pilgrims that includes a Grail Reliquae benefit from Blessings of the Lady, or just the Grail Reliquae itself?
Ruling: If the unit includes a Grail Reliquae, the entire unit gains Blessings of the Lady.

Question: Are the effects of the Casket of Souls' Bound spell 'Light of Protection' cumulative?
Ruling: No.

Question: Are unsaved wounds caused by the mount of a model bearing the Laurels of Victory worth 2 combat result points?
Ruling: No, only unsaved wounds caused by the bearer (the rider) count.

Question: What happens to a Fanatic that ends its movement within the Command range of one or more models with the Hostile Terrain special rule?
Ruling: The Fanatic must make a Dangerous Terrain test. Rather than creating an area of dangerous terrain, Hostile Terrain represents a model laying traps and creating hazards, causing enemy models to make a dangerous terrain test should they end their movement within that area.

Question: Can a cannon be shot in such a way as to hit an enemy unit that is engaged in combat with a friendly unit?
Ruling: No. Page 143 of the rulebook makes it clear that, except in rare cases, units cannot shoot enemy units that are engaged in combat. In the case of cannon, this means the target point cannot be placed in such a way as to risk the cannonball hitting a friendly unit, or an enemy unit engaged in combat with a friendly unit.

Question: When a character takes a chariot as a mount, do they replace one of the crew?
Ruling: No. The points you pay for a chariot include its crew, whether that chariot is included in your army on its own or as a mount for a character. However, in reality it might prove difficult to fit a character and the full complement of crew into the chariot model itself. If so, it is perfectly acceptable to remove one or more of the crew models to make space for the character. In such cases, we can think of the missing crew model's profile(s) as a way of representing that the beasts pulling a character's chariot are bound to be bigger, stronger and better trained than normal.

Question: If a model has Armour Bane (X) listed amongst its special rules (i.e., if the model has the special rule itself rather than a weapon it carries having it), does it apply to Impact Hits or Stomp Attacks?
Ruling: Yes.

Question: If a unit with the Press of Battle rule has not yet fought, models from the end of the first fighting rank will 'close in' as described on page 150, into base contact with the enemy. But can models from the second fighting rank 'step forward' into base contact and fight immediately?
Ruling: Yes. As stated on page 150, models cannot fight during a phase in which they stepped forward into a fighting rank. However, models already in a fighting rank can step forward and close in as described, maximising their number of Attacks.

Question: Models cannot cast Magic Missiles or Magical Vortexes after marching, but does this include Bound spells?
Ruling: Yes.

Question: If a Wizard has a magic item or special rule that allows them to re-roll a failed Casting roll, can they re-roll a natural double 1 and avoid a Miscast?
Ruling: No. A roll of a natural double 1 isn't merely a failed Casting roll, it is a Miscast, as described on page 109.

Question: What happens if a scatter roll causes any part of an object to cross beyond the edge of the battlefield?
Ruling: The object is removed from play.

Question: Can a Troll Hag be the General of an Orc and Goblin Tribes army made using the Grand Army composition list?
Ruling: No. A Troll Hag is a Rare choice in the Orc and Goblin Tribes Grand Army composition list. She can, however, be the General of a Troll Horde.

Question: Does a magic standard that affects a unit's weapons (the Razor Standard, for example) also make those weapons magical, giving them the Magical Attacks special rule?
Ruling: Not unless the description of the magic standard in question states that the weapons of a unit carrying it gain the Magical Attacks special rule. Generally speaking, purchasing a magic item doesn't conjure up additional bonuses from the æther.

Question: Can the spell Spectral Doppelganger from the Lore of Illusion be used with a magic weapon that allows the wielder to make only a single attack?
Ruling: No. Weapons limited to a single attack can only inflict a single hit.

Question: Can a Doomseeker join a unit of Slayers?
Ruling: No, as per the errata, a Doomseeker is not a character. They are loners and outcasts even amongst Slayers and, as such, act as a unit of one model.

Question: Do the points I spend on Core units within an allied contingent count towards the minimum percentage of Core units overall?
Ruling: No.

Question: Two characters are engaged in a challenge whilst their units battle around them. At the end of the round, the losing unit might Fall Back in Good Order or Give Ground. If their enemy pursues or follows up, does the challenge continue?
Ruling: Yes. As stated on page 211, if both participants in a challenge survive the round and if the combat continues, the challenge continues.

Question: Is a unit's maximum possible charge range the maximum distance from an enemy unit at which it can declare a charge, or the maximum distance it can move when making a charge move?
Ruling: It is the maximum distance from an enemy unit at which it can declare a charge.

Question: Do Skirmishers have flank or rear arcs whilst engaged in combat?
Ruling: Whilst Skirmishers do form up when engaged in combat, they are not considered to have flank or rear arcs for the purposes of calculating combat result points.

Question: Does Press of Battle apply to a unit's flank and rear arcs, or just to its front arc?
Ruling: If a unit has and is able to use the Press of Battle rule, it can do so regardless of which of its arcs the enemy is engaged with.

Question: Can a Casket of Souls move at the end of the Shooting phase of its turn using the Reserve Move special rule (should it have it)?
Ruling: No.

Question: How does the Spectral Doppelganger spell interact with weapons that have either the Strike First or Strike Last special rule?
Ruling: The spell is cast at the Wizard's Initiative, meaning attacks generated by the spell are made at the Wizard's Initiative. However, if the casting Wizard wishes to use a weapon with the Strike Last special rule, those attacks are made at Initiative 1.

Question: When a unit performs a manoeuvre, can its front edge pass through another unit?
Ruling: No. The only exception to this is when a unit pivots.

Question: When a Goblin Hewer shoots using the Whirling Death special rule, does it add a D3 modifier to the number of shots rolled for each rank or file, or just a single D3 modifier?
Ruling: Roll an Artillery dice, plus an extra D3 per rank or file of the unit, depending upon which arc the weapon is shooting into.

Question: Can any type of cannon fire grapeshot?
Ruling: Only cannons or weapons that fire using the 'Cannon Fire' special rule may also fire 'Grapeshot', as described on page 227 of the *Warhammer: The Old World* rulebook. This is in addition to any other special rules or additional modes of fire the weapon may have.

Question: Some mounted models have the Counter Charge special rule but others do not, even though they have the same type of mount. Is this intentional?
Ruling: Yes. Counter Charge is a rule that represents the skill and ferocity of the rider, not their mount. In other words, not every rider is willing or able to perform a counter charge, regardless of their mount.

Question: If a Troll Hag purchases a magic weapon, are any of its special rules conferred onto Motherly Love attacks?
Ruling: No. If she attacks normally, she can use her magic weapon. If she makes a Motherly Love attack, she does not use her magic weapon.

Question: If I upgrade a unit of Boar Boyz to be Big 'Uns, do their War Boars benefit as well?
Ruling:
Yes.

Note that the Strength characteristic of Big 'Uns is modified whilst they are engaged in combat, and that Impact Hits are made using the model's unmodified Strength characteristic.

Question: If a model is required to make a Leadership test using its own Leadership characteristic, can it use the Leadership of a different model, the General for example, instead?
Ruling: No. When the rules state a model must make a Leadership test using its own Leadership, it must use its own Leadership.

Question: If a spell has two Casting Values, do I have to say which I'm attempting to cast the spell at before making my Casting roll?
Ruling: No, your casting result determines the 'strength' of the spell. In other words, the higher your casting result, the more power the spell will have and the greater its effect will be.

Question: A character mounted on a ridden monster or a chariot can choose to use their own or their mount's armour value, whichever is better. If the character wears magic armour but I choose to use the mount's armour value, can I still claim other benefits conferred by the magic armour?
Ruling: No. You must use a magic item fully or not at all.

Question: Does a spell cast on a Regimental Unit affect its Detachments, or vice versa?
Ruling: No, spells that affect a unit only affect the unit they are cast on.

Question: Can the wearer of the Wizarding Hat cast spells whilst wearing armour?
Ruling: Yes. The wearer of the Wizarding Hat is not actually a Wizard – their magical powers are granted by a haunted hat which is not affected by any armour the model may wear.

Question: What happens if a unit in Lance formation that declares a charge finds its movement blocked by the presence of an enemy unit to its flank, where the unit gets wider?
Ruling: Such situations are covered by the rules for Accidental Contact During a Charge. If the Lance can wheel around the enemy unit, it should do so. If not, the Lance has two choices; halting its charge or continuing ahead and making contact with the enemy unit, treating it as a redirected charge.

Question: If a unit bearing a standard inscribed with the Master Rune of Hesitation Falls Back in Good Order and is pursued and caught by an enemy unit, does the rune take effect?
Ruling: Yes. When a pursuing unit catches an enemy unit that Fell Back in Good Order, it counts as having charged that unit.

Question: If a model bearing the Laurels of Victory Stands & Shoots as a charge reaction, causing one or more unsaved wounds, are those unsaved wounds each worth 2 combat result points?
Ruling: No.

Question: Can a unit that is partially on a hill shoot in two ranks?
Ruling: No. To claim the benefits of being on a hill, a unit must be entirely on the hill.

Question: If a character is within one fighting rank they cannot move through the ranks to join another. Might this prevent them from accepting a challenge?
Ruling: No. If a character is eligible to accept a challenge they can do so wherever they are in a unit and will move through the ranks into base contact with their opponent. However, if it is awkward to move a model, it is quite acceptable for the players to agree it has moved and fight the challenge as if the combatants were in base contact, thus avoiding too much disruption.

Question: When a unit of Skirmishers becomes engaged in combat and forms up, must any command group models it contains be placed in the fighting rank?
Ruling: Yes.

Question: When a unit wheels, is it acceptable for a rear corner to pass through another unit?
Ruling: Yes, provided the unit does not end its movement 'on top' of another unit or within 1" of an enemy unit.

Question: Is it possible to resurrect models in a unit of Skirmishers?
Ruling: Yes, simply place the resurrected models in coherency (i.e., within 1" of another model) with the rest of the unit.

Question: Does the Griffon Standard allow a unit to claim a higher Rank Bonus than normal for its troop type?
Ruling: Yes. As stated in the item's rules, a unit carrying the Griffon Standard can claim a Rank Bonus of +2 for each extra rank behind the first, rather than the usual +1, meaning a unit with two extra ranks could claim a Rank Bonus of +4, rather than the usual +2.

Question: If a unit of enemy infantry charges a unit with the Master Rune of Hesitation, can it make use of the Press of Battle rule to fight in two ranks?
Ruling: No. Although the Rune prevents a charging enemy unit from using certain weapons or special rules, the unit has still charged, and thus cannot make use of the Press of Battle rule.

Question: Can the wearer of the Wizarding Hat also wear a magic helmet, such as the Bedazzling Helm?
Ruling: Yes, because one is an enchanted item, the other is a type of magic armour, but we hope anyone equipping a model in such a way would make the effort to depict it wearing two hats!

Question: Can a war machine shoot using the Ballistic Skill of a character that has joined it?
Ruling: No. Because a war machine and its crew are treated as a single model, you must use the crew's BS.

Question: If I have a character with an armour value of 6+ mounted on a chariot with an armour value of 4+, for example, am I obliged to use the chariot's armour value?
Ruling: No, you choose whichever armour value is better. However, allowing for magical armour and other special rules, 'better' is somewhat subjective. Obviously an armour value of 4+ is better than one of 6+ but there is often more to deciding which armour to use than just the armour value it offers, many types of magic armour confer additional bonuses that make them better. Basically, when the rules say 'choose', they are giving you a choice.

Question: When a unit Counter Charges, it rolls D3+1 to determine how far it moves. Is this roll counted as a Charge roll?
Ruling: No.

Question: How many attacks can a model with a split profile make if it is in the fighting rank but not in base contact with the enemy?
Ruling: A model with a split profile consists of not one model, but several, all sharing the same base. Therefore, each model on that base could make a single attack. In the case of a cavalry model, for example, this would be one attack from the rider and one from their mount.

Question: Can a unit on a hill draw a line of sight across and shoot over another unit on the same hill?
Ruling: A unit that is closer to the top of a hill (i.e., the centre of the hill or the edge of the battlefield) can draw a line of sight across and shoot over one that is closer to the bottom. Units cannot draw a line of sight across or shoot over units that are closer to the top of a hill than they are.

Question: If a Remains in Play spell with two Casting Values is cast at the higher value, which is used when trying to dispel it during the Conjuration sub-phase?
Ruling: As stated on page 111, in order to dispel a Remains in Play spell during your Conjuration sub-phase, you must beat the minimum casting value given in the spell's description. This is the case even if the spell was cast at the higher of two given casting values.

Question: When shooting a Doom Diver catapult, the template can be moved D3" after scattering. Can I use this to move the template so that it hits an enemy character that is within 3" of a unit, a character that could not usually be targeted by shooting?
Ruling: Yes. The template must be moved the full distance rolled on the D3 but, if that allows you to position it to hit an enemy character, you may do so. Sneaky Goblin Doom Divers steer their flight in an attempt to hit the best possible target, so this is completely in character.

Question: Can the size of a range 'self' spell's aura of effect be increased by the Idol of Gork?
Ruling: No. The aura of effect of a range 'self' spell is not its range.

Question: Some single use special rules and magic items require a Leadership test to use. Do they count as having been used even if this test is failed?
Ruling: Yes.

Question: How does a bolt thrower work when shooting at a unit in Lance formation?
Ruling: The number of models hit is based on the number of ranks overall. For example, a Lance of six knights (arranged in ranks  of one, two and three models) would suffer three hits. When a Lance is shot in its flank by a bolt thrower, the number of hits is based on the widest file. To continue the example above, three models would be hit based on the depth of the unit.

Question: If a unit of enemy infantry charges a unit with the Master Rune of Hesitation, does it gain the Initiative bonus for charging?
Ruling: Yes. The Master Rune of Hesitation only prevents the use of certain weapons and special rules.

Question: If two units are engaged across a low linear obstacle, are they limited to making just a single attack because they aren't in base contact?
Ruling: No. Whilst a charging unit will become disordered, and whilst Impact Hits and Stomp Attacks cannot be made due to the presence of the obstacle (as stated above), units are otherwise able to fight normally across a low linear obstacle, as if they were in base contact.

Question: Some war machines can have additional models attached to them, such as the Orc Bully. If the war machine is destroyed, are any attached models also destroyed?
Ruling: Yes.

Question: Is there a maximum beyond which characteristics cannot be modified?
Ruling: Unless a rule specifies a maximum, no.

Question: If a character whose mount has a different sized base to the models in a unit making up a Lance formation wishes to join that unit, where should I place the model?
Ruling: The Lance formation offers a bit more flexibility than other formations. For example, it is perfectly acceptable to place a character such as a Duke or a Baron at the front of the Lance should you wish. In the case of a Handmaiden of the Lady, the Shield of the Lady special rule allows such models to be placed  at the rear of such units. Alternatively, they can be placed within the unit. In this case, the extra base size will make very little difference to the shape of the unit.

Question: If a Wizard wears the Wizarding Hat, does it increase their Level of Wizardry?
Ruling: No. As stated in the item's description, the wearer of the Wizarding Hat is a Level 1 Wizard and knows one randomly generated spell. This is clearly a huge detriment to a powerful Wizard, but might be a boon to any character that is not a Wizard.

Question: If a unit charged by two or more enemy units Counter Charges one of them, it may end its movement presenting a different arc to the other charging unit(s). Do those units resolve their charges against those arcs?
Ruling: Yes. When a unit Counter Charges, it risks exposing its flanks or rear to the enemy, such are the perils of bravado.

Question: Some chariots are equipped with large scale missile weapons such as bolt throwers. Who shoots such weapons; the crew, the beasts that draw the chariot, the chariot itself, or a character mounted upon the chariot?
Ruling: Missile weapons mounted on chariots (or howdahs) are shot by the crew, using their Ballistic Skill.

Question: When a unit wheels, do you have to measure the curvature of its movement?
Ruling: No, simply measure the unit’s movement in a straight line from the end of the front rank furthest from the corner around which the unit pivots.

Question: All Goblins Fear Elves. If a unit of Elves causes Fear, does this lead them to cause Terror in Goblins?
Ruling: No.

Question: If a character mounted on a ridden monster or chariot carries a shield, does that improve the mount's armour value?
Ruling: No, a shield is carried by the character, not the mount.

Question: How many Remains in Play spells can I attempt to dispel during my Conjuration sub-phase?
Ruling: As many as you wish, or, perhaps more accurately, as many as your opponent has in play and as many as you are able.

Question: Does the presence in a unit of a character whose base takes up the space of two or more models in two or more ranks reduce that unit’s rank bonus?
Ruling: No.

Question: Can a Drilled unit redress the ranks before making a Counter Charge charge reaction?
Ruling: Yes.

Question: When a unit in Lance formation is engaged in combat, every model on the outside counts as being in base contact. How many enemy models count as being in base contact with the Lance?
Ruling:
Every model within the first fighting rank that is within a number of inches equal to its Movement characteristic of the Lance. In the case of enemy regular or heavy infantry, the second fighting rank is not in base contact – there is another rank in the way.

When a Lance charges, it pierces deep into the enemy formation, pushing warriors back and causing the enemy lines to close around it. It’s very hard to show this on the table though, hence the abstraction.

Note that this can create an area of ‘dead ground’ between a Lance and a unit it is engaged in combat with. If any enemy units are caught within this, refer to the rules covering ‘accidental contact’ on page 131 of the Warhammer: the Old World rulebook.

Question: Do potions affect a model's mount?
Ruling: No.

Question: Can the Glowy Green Amulet be used by a character that isn't a Wizard?
Ruling: Yes. The Glowy Green Amulet is a talisman, meaning any character that can take magic items can take it. However, if they wish to use it against an enemy spell, they do so instead of a Wizardly dispel attempt being made. This means that you cannot also attempt a Wizardly dispel against a spell you use the Glowy Green Amulet against, even if the Glowy Green Amulet explodes.

Question: If a unit will have to wheel before or during a charge, do I have to allow for that when declaring and measuring the charge?
Ruling: Yes. Wheeling during a charge is part of the charge move. The free wheel to align once contact is made is free.

Question: What happens to a Remains in Play spell that is already in effect if the Wizard that cast it attempts to cast it again?
Ruling: It ends immediately.

Question: Can a Close Order unit of just one model claim the Close Order combat result bonus?
Ruling: Yes, provided it has a high enough Unit Strength (as per the errata on page 1). A unit of just one model is still a unit.

Question: Can a unit arrayed in Close Order or Open Order formation be one model wide?
Ruling: Yes.

Question: If some of my opponent’s attacks cause multiple Wounds to be lost per unsaved wound they cause, in what order are those unsaved wounds applied to my unit?
Ruling:
Apply unsaved wounds to a unit one at a time and one model at a time. When a model is reduced to zero Wounds on its profile, it is removed from play as a casualty (as described on page 102). If a model loses more Wounds than it has on its profile, the excess wounds are lost – they do not spill over onto other models in the same unit.

With this in mind, apply unsaved wounds that cause models to lose all of their remaining Wounds first (Killing Blows and Monster Slaying Blows, for example), then unsaved wounds that cause multiple Wounds to be lost (Multiple Wounds (X), for example), then, finally, unsaved wounds that cause a single Wound to be lost.

Question: Is a charging Lance blunted if an enemy unit counter charges it?
Ruling: No. As both units are charging, the clause that a Lance is blunted if it is charged and does not counter charge is negated.

Question: If the Scroll of Transmogrification is successfully used against a Wizard mounted on a ridden monster (a Dragon, for example), what happens to the mount?
Ruling: The Wizard is transmogrified, but not their mount. In the example given, you would be left with a Frog riding a Dragon.

Question: A Clumsy unit cannot be joined by a character that is not also Clumsy, but can a Clumsy character join a unit that is not Clumsy?
Ruling: Yes.

Question: What happens to a unit that Gives Ground whilst within 2" of the edge of the battlefield?
Ruling: Should any part of a unit cross beyond the edge of the battlefield whilst it is Giving Ground, the entire unit is removed from play and counts as having been destroyed.

Question: Can a model wearing armour or carrying a shield cast a Bound spell?
Ruling: Yes.

Question: If a unit whose troop type is 'infantry' that has been joined by a character whose troop type is 'cavalry' charges an enemy unit with the Counter Charge special rule, can that unit Counter Charge?
Ruling: No. A unit's troop type doesn't change when joined by a character.

Question: When a unit redresses the ranks, must the width of its front rank be increased or decreased as equally as possible on either side?
Ruling: Yes. The exception to this is when the width of the front rank is increased or decreased by an odd number of models. In such cases, one side of the unit will gain or lose one more model than the other side.

Question: What happens if a Scroll of Transmogrification is used on a Bound spell?
Ruling: After testing against the item's Power Level (in place of its Level of Wizardry), it may be turned into an inanimate frog, rendering it useless until it turns back. During each Start of Turn sub-phase, you may roll a D6 for each transmogrified item in your army to see if it returns to normal, as described on page 343.

Question: Can a unit with the Finest Warhorses special rule re-roll the dice when using Swiftstride?
Ruling: No. Finest Warhorses allows a unit to re-roll its Charge roll, but the D6 rolled when using Swiftstride is not part of the charge roll; it is rolled to give a modifier to the result of the Charge roll.

Question: Does a unit that is joined by a character of a different troop type gain the rules associated with the character’s troop type?
Ruling: No.

Question: How far does a model with the Random Movement special rule move when making a Counter Charge?
Ruling: As stated in the Counter Charge special rule, a model that makes a Counter Charge moves D3+1".

Question: What happens to a unit that cannot Give Ground due to the presence of another unit?
Ruling: The unit's movement stops immediately, as if it were surrounded.

Question: Does a unit that has to declare a charge due to being Frenzied or Impetuous have to do so if a friendly unit of Skirmishers lies between it and a potential charge target, obstructing its movement?
Ruling: If there is a chance of the Skirmishers moving so that they are no longer an obstruction (if they declare a charge, for example), yes. Otherwise, no.

Question: Can a Wizard attempt to dispel a Bound spell by attempting a Wizardly dispel?
Ruling: If the Wizard is within range of the model casting the Bound spell and not otherwise prevented from attempting a Wizardly dispel, yes. As stated on page 109, you may attempt to dispel a Bound spell as usual.

Question: Can models choose not to make Armour, Ward or Regeneration saves if it has them?
Ruling: No. If a model can attempt to make a save, it must.

Question: Can a Wizard with a physical attribute that 'counts as' a type of armour (such as a Treeman Ancient's arboreal armour) make Casting or Dispel rolls?
Ruling: Yes. Whilst such attributes are as protective as a suit of armour, such models do not wear armour.

Question: Can a Wizard with a Lore Familiar choose one of their faction's signature spells instead of the signature spell of their chosen lore?
Ruling: No.

Question: Can a character who is within the fighting rank of their unit but not in base contact with the enemy move through the ranks so that they are?
Ruling: No. Characters can move through the ranks into the fighting rank, but cannot move within the fighting rank.

Question: A pursuing unit must move directly towards the fleeing enemy, but must it move forwards whilst doing so, or can it move sideways?
Ruling: As stated on page 123, units must move forwards unless performing a manoeuvre (or when Giving Ground). This includes whilst pursuing.

Question: Although it cannot make a charge move, a unit in Marching Column can declare a charge. Why is this?
Ruling:
There are several reasons. Firstly, a Drilled unit that declares a charge whilst in Marching Column can freely redress its ranks to adopt Combat Order after determining its charge range, but before moving, thus allowing it to make a charge move.

Secondly, units that are obliged to declare a charge in certain circumstances (those that are Frenzied or Impetuous, for example) must do so even whilst in Marching Column. If they cannot make the charge move, they don't move at all and the charge is failed. This prevents Marching Column being used to avoid declaring compulsory charges.

Alternatively, there might be a psychological advantage to declaring a charge with a Marching Column. For example, the unit might cause Terror, or the charge target might already be fleeing.

Of course, it isn't easy to set up situations where such tactics can be used and therein lies the challenge.

Question: If a unit with the Press of Battle rule has two fighting ranks, can I remove casualties from the second rank?
Ruling: No. Models in the first fighting rank, the rank in base contact with the enemy, fall first as casualties.

Question: Can a Drilled unit redress the ranks before Giving Ground?
Ruling:
Yes. A unit that Gives Ground is not a fleeing unit.

Note that, as mentioned previously, should any part of a unit cross beyond the edge of the battlefield whilst it is Giving Ground, the entire unit is removed from play and counts as having been destroyed. It is intentional that a Drilled unit might be able to avoid this fate.

Question: How many spells does a Wizard with an Arcane Familiar know? For example, does a Level 3 Wizard know three spells from two Lores (two from one and one from the other), or six spells, three from each Lore?
Ruling: An Arcane Familiar does not increase the number of spells a Wizard knows, it simply allows them to know spells from two Lores. Thus a Level 3 Wizard would know three spells from two Lores.

Question: If a unit has to pivot before fleeing from an enemy it is engaged in combat with, must it make Peril tests?
Ruling: No. As stated on page 125, units ignore other units whilst pivoting.

Question: Can an Evasive unit use that special rule whilst engaged in combat or whilst fleeing?
Ruling: No.

Question: If a unit contains models of two different troop types, how do I determine its maximum rank bonus?
Ruling: In such cases, the troop type of the majority of the models determines the unit’s maximum rank bonus.

Question: Can a character be placed amongst a unit's command group?
Ruling: Yes.

Question: If a Drilled unit in Marching Column has to declare a charge due to being Frenzied or Impetuous, can it choose not to use Drilled to redress the ranks and adopt combat order?
Ruling: If it is able to redress the ranks (i.e., if there is space for it to do so), no. A unit that is obliged to charge must endeavour to make use of any special rules it has in order to charge. The unit just really wants to charge, and it'll play this game without you if it has to!

Question: If a Wizard has joined a unit, can they cast spells from any rank, or must they be in the front rank?
Ruling: Unless they have a special rule that states otherwise, a Wizard must be in the front rank (or the first fighting rank) of their unit to cast spells. Like all characters, Wizards bring no benefit to their unit by skulking in the rear ranks.

Question: If I want to charge an enemy unit that is a Large Target with a unit of mine that is in its front arc (for example) but cannot because the enemy unit is already engaged in its front arc, can I instead charge its flank?
Ruling: No. Sometimes a charge isn't possible.

Question: If there is no space for a character in the front rank of a unit with the Press of Battle rule, can they join the second rank?
Ruling: No, characters must be placed in the front rank. If this is not possible, they retire to the rear.

Question: Some models can be found in one faction's army list, but can be included in an army made using a composition list belonging to a different faction (Dragon Ogre Shaggoths, or units that can be included as Mercenaries, for example). What lists of magic items do such models have access to?
Ruling: Models can purchase magic items from the list of common magic items in the Warhammer: the Old World rulebook, or from their own faction's list of magic items. A Dragon Ogre Shaggoth, for example, can purchase items from the common or Beastmen Brayherds magic item lists.

Question: Do effects that modify a model's Movement characteristic also modify how far a model with the Fly (X) special rule can fly?
Ruling: Yes. If a model has the Fly (X) special rule, the number given in brackets is essentially a second Movement characteristic. Any effect that modifies one will modify both.

Question: What happens if a unit that wishes to make a pursuit or overrun move cannot move due to the presence of other units?
Ruling: It may happen that it is simply impossible for a pursuing or overrunning unit to move without it ending up 'on top' of another unit. In such cases, the unit does not move, but is considered to have made a pursuit or overrun move.

Question: Does a Wizard that has joined a unit need to be in base contact with an enemy model to cast an Assailment spell, or do they only need to be within the fighting rank?
Ruling: They do not need to be in base contact, but they must be in the first fighting rank.

Question: How does a Close Order unit of just one model act, is it still a Close Order formation, or does it act like a Skirmisher?
Ruling: A Close Order unit always acts as such, even if it only contains a single model.

Question: If a Wizard declines a challenge and retires from combat, does their unit lose the benefits of any range 'Self' spells that Wizard has cast?
Ruling: Yes.

Question: A fighting rank cannot contain more characters than it does rank and file models. In the case of a unit with the Press of Battle rule, does this include rank and file models in a second fighting rank?
Ruling: No. No single fighting rank can contain more characters than it does rank and file models. It doesn’t matter how many fighting ranks a unit might have.

Question: Can a model with two versions of the Fly (X) special rule combine both and fly further?
Ruling: No. A model that has more than one version of the Fly (X) special rule essentially has two Movement characteristics it can use when flying. Of these, you may use the best.

Question: If a unit completely destroys its enemy in combat and makes an overrun move, can it attempt to reform after moving?
Ruling: Unless it pursued into a fresh enemy, yes. A unit that overruns makes a normal pursuit move and, since its enemy has already been wiped out, it may attempt to reform as if it had run down its foe, as described on page 129.

Question: If a single model unit straddles two arcs of an enemy unit it wishes to charge, is it always considered to be in the arc that gives the least advantage?
Ruling: No, this is only the case when you cannot determine which arc of an enemy unit a charging unit is within. If it is clear that the majority of a charging unit is within one particular arc, even if that unit consists of only one model, it will charge into that arc.

Question: Does a unit count as being obscured when some of the models within it are behind others?
Ruling: No. A unit cannot be obscured from the enemy by itself. What’s more, models within a unit do not obscure the enemy from other models within the same unit. They either completely block line of sight, or present no obstruction.

Question: If a unit with the Fly (X) special rule moves over a magical vortex that counts as dangerous terrain, is it affected by it?
Ruling: Yes. Magical vortexes are considered tall enough to affect even models that are flying high above the battlefield.

Question: Can characters displace command group models into the second rank of a unit with the Press of Battle rule?
Ruling: No, command group models must always be in the front rank of their unit.

Question: If a unit with the Fly (X) special rule is engaged in combat, can it use its 'Fly Movement' characteristic when determining which models are close enough to models within the enemy unit to fight or make supporting attacks?
Ruling: No. Models with the Fly (X) special rule only fly whilst moving. In other words, such models are considered to have landed on the ground whilst the fighting takes place, and must use their given Movement characteristic to determine if they are close enough to the enemy to fight.

Question: On page 157 it states that units that pursue and catch an enemy that Fell Back in Good Order count as having charged during the next turn, but what exactly does this mean?
Ruling: Exactly what it says – the pursuing unit counts as having charged its enemy during the next turn of the game, when the combat is fought, even though the unit will not actually have moved during that turn. This means rules and weapons that can only be used by charging models can be used, that Initiative modifiers for charging are granted (based on the distance the unit pursued), and so forth.

Question: If a unit charges an enemy that is defending a low linear obstacle, can it stop on top of the obstacle?
Ruling: No. As stated on page 270, the charging unit moves into base contact with the obstacle.

Question: Can different saves be combined together to improve their save value? For example, if a model has two Ward saves, can they be combined to give a single Ward save with a better Warding value?
Ruling: No, values given as a target number cannot be combined to lower the target number. If a model has two or more Ward saves, as per the example, simply use the best.

Question: If a model with a split profile has the Impact Hits (X) special rule, do all parts of the model cause Impact Hits?
Ruling: No. Impact Hits are only made by a mount, not by its rider(s). In the case of a chariot, Impact Hits are made by the chariot itself, not by the beasts that draw it. If a rider has their own Impact Hits (X) special rule, these are made separately by the rider.

Question: If a character is in any rank of a unit other than the front rank (or the first fighting rank, in the case of units engaged in combat), for any reason, do they confer any bonuses onto the unit?
Ruling: No, not unless they have a special rule stating otherwise. Characters must lead from the front or retire to the rear.

Question: When a unit redirects a charge, can it charge a unit that lies beyond its maximum possible charge range?
Ruling: No.

Question: Whilst running down the foe, is a charging unit considered to be pursuing a fleeing enemy for the purposes of crossing the edge of the battlefield, etc.?
Ruling: Yes, a unit that runs down the foe is very much pursuing a fleeing enemy whilst doing so.

Question: If a model has Killing Blow or Monster Slayer, does a roll To Wound of a natural 6 cause an enemy to lose all of its remaining Wounds even if that enemy would normally be too tough to wound?
Ruling: No. If a model cannot wound an enemy, it cannot kill it.

Question: If a Warband character (as described on page 180) joins a Warband with a Rank Bonus of one or more, does the modifier to their Leadership characteristic increase their Command range?
Ruling: Yes.

Question: When a unit enters the battle as reinforcements, is there a limit to how far onto the battlefield models can be placed?
Ruling: Yes. The unit is considered to have moved onto the battlefield. Therefore, no model can be placed more than twice its Movement characteristic from the edge of the battlefield its unit enters from.
